ABOUT:
Wynwood House is a hospitality and real estate platform operating across seven countries in Latin America and Europe. It blends hospitality, local expertise, and real estate to help guests live like locals with the consistency and comfort of home.
FOUNDED:
2019
USING CONDUIT SINCE:
October 2025
“You cannot tell the difference between an AI agent and a human agent.”
Mayra
Global Head of Customer Experience, Wynwood House
About Wynwood House
Hospitality and real estate platform helping people feel at home wherever they go
From business travelers relocating to a new city to families seeking a longer stay abroad, Wynwood House has built its brand around a simple idea: everyone deserves to feel at home wherever they are.
Operating across seven countries throughout Latin America and Europe, Wynwood House combines hospitality, local expertise, and real estate experience to help guests live like locals while enjoying the consistency and comfort of home.
As the company expanded across multiple markets, maintaining a consistent guest experience became increasingly challenging. Every new city brought additional guests, languages, and operational complexity—but the expectation remained the same: fast, thoughtful service that felt personal.
"We needed faster responses, better visibility, and a way to manage everything without jumping between multiple tools," said Mayra, Global Head of Customer Experience at Wynwood House.
Rather than continuing to layer new processes on top of existing systems, Wynwood House made the decision to move its guest communication operation to Conduit.
The Challenge
For a hospitality company operating across multiple countries and languages, communication isn't just a support function—it's a core part of the guest experience.
Before Conduit, Wynwood House's customer experience team relied on a collection of disconnected tools to manage guest communications:
Guesty for guest messaging
ChatGPT for drafting responses
Separate translation tools for multilingual communication
Google Sheets for sentiment tracking and reporting
As the company grew, several operational challenges became impossible to ignore.
Fragmented Workflows
Agents constantly switched between platforms to draft messages, translate responses, review guest history, and track performance metrics.
Instead of focusing on guests, teams spent valuable time navigating between systems.
Slow Resolution Times
When Mayra joined Wynwood House, guests were waiting an average of 14–15 minutes for issue resolution.
As booking volume increased across multiple countries, maintaining response quality while improving speed became increasingly difficult.
Manual Sentiment Tracking
Customer sentiment was tracked manually through shared spreadsheets and agent-generated scores.
"The sentiment, for us, we did it manually," Mayra explained. "We had a Google Sheet from one to five, and it depended on the criteria each agent had."
The process was time-consuming, inconsistent, and difficult to trust.
Poor Shift Handoffs
With teams operating across time zones and multiple countries, agents often needed to read entire conversation histories before taking ownership of a guest issue.
Critical context could easily be lost between shifts.
Limited Visibility
Managers lacked reliable ways to measure guest sentiment, identify coaching opportunities, and understand how effectively the team was serving guests at scale.
The Solution
When Wynwood House implemented Conduit, the impact was immediately visible—not only in internal operations, but in the quality of guest conversations themselves.
"The first thing we noticed was the quality of the AI replies," said Mayra. "You cannot tell the difference between an AI agent and a human agent."
Rather than relying on multiple disconnected tools, Wynwood House consolidated guest communication into a single platform.
One Unified Inbox
Drafting, translation, sentiment analysis, tagging, internal notes, follow-ups, and guest messaging were all centralized within Conduit.
This eliminated constant context switching and gave agents a complete view of every guest interaction.
AI-Powered Multilingual Communication
Before Conduit, agents relied on literal machine translations that often lost context and tone.
Today, guests receive responses that feel natural, personalized, and written in their own language.
"I work with ChatGPT and other AI tools every day, and sometimes you can immediately tell it's AI," said Mayra. "With Conduit, we're not seeing that. It feels like a full conversation with a human."
Smarter Conversation Management
Instead of simply archiving conversations, agents can now:
Resolve and close conversations properly
Schedule follow-ups
Track guest registration workflows
Manage operational processes through tags
Create accountability across shifts
AI-Powered Shift Handoffs
One of the most significant improvements came during shift changes.
Previously, agents needed to read entire message threads to understand a guest issue before taking over.
Now, AI-generated summaries provide instant context.
"The AI already did it for me," said Mayra. "I'm just going to focus on finding the solution."
Instead of spending time reconstructing conversations, agents can immediately focus on helping guests.
The Impact
Since implementing Conduit, Wynwood House has transformed how its customer experience team operates.
More Time Focused on Guests
By consolidating communication, translation, guest context, and sentiment tracking into a single platform, agents spend less time managing tools and more time helping guests.
Tasks that previously required multiple systems can now be completed from one workspace.
Stronger Visibility Into Guest Experience
Manual spreadsheets have been replaced by AI-generated sentiment analysis, giving managers a more accurate picture of guest satisfaction.
Every week, the team reviews conversations with lower sentiment scores to identify coaching opportunities, improve empathy, and create better guest outcomes.
What was once an unreliable reporting process is now becoming a core customer experience KPI.
Scaling Across 7 Countries While Maintaining Service Quality
As Wynwood House expanded across Latin America and Europe, maintaining a consistent guest experience became increasingly challenging. By centralizing guest communication in Conduit, the team built a standardized operation that supports growth across seven countries while maintaining service quality.
Today, Wynwood House manages thousands of guest interactions with greater consistency and efficiency, helping sustain strong guest satisfaction scores, including a 4.8 Airbnb rating in Colombia.
Looking Ahead
For Wynwood House, AI isn't replacing hospitality—it's helping the team deliver it more consistently as the company grows.
The company is continuing to expand across markets while refining how guest communication, operational workflows, and customer experience teams work together.
They're also preparing to bring additional communication channels into Conduit, further consolidating guest interactions into a single platform.
By replacing fragmented workflows with a hospitality-focused communication platform, Wynwood House has reduced guest resolution times from 15 minutes to 3, improved operational visibility, and built a scalable foundation for growth across seven countries.

From luxury beachfront villas in Aruba to curated stays in Curaçao, Bocobay has built its reputation on exceptional guest service, personalized owner communication, and smooth operational execution.
For years, the team had relied on Intercom to manage guest messaging. But as guest interactions grew more complex, it became clear that a general-purpose support tool wasn’t built for the realities of hospitality.
“We needed a system that could handle the complexity of guest interactions, owner relations, and on-the-ground operations—all in one place,” said Nick Curtis, co-founder of Bocobay.
Instead of forcing Intercom to fit their needs, Bocobay made a decisive move: they migrated their entire guest and owner communication workflow to Conduit.
The Problem
For a high-end hospitality brand, fragmented communication isn’t just an inconvenience—it’s a threat to the guest experience.
Bocobay’s team had been juggling:
WhatsApp for guest and owner messaging
A separate support inbox for external conversations
Hostaway's inbox for Airbnb and direct reservations
“It’s always been painful having two inboxes,” Nick recalled. “We needed a way to unify everything.”
Their biggest challenges:
Scattered communication channels
– Conversations were spread across multiple tools, making it hard to maintain a consistent guest experience.
Lack of visibility
– The team had no easy way to track response times, agent performance, or guest satisfaction.
Limited scalability
– Their current setup worked—for now. But as they expanded to new markets, they needed a solution built for the complexity of vacation rentals.
The Solution
When Bocobay discovered Conduit, it wasn’t just about bringing messages into one place—it was about elevating their entire approach to guest communication.
“As soon as we saw Conduit could handle everything reliably, moving over was an easy decision. We wanted one inbox, not two,” said Nick.
Instead of a disruptive overhaul, the migration was deliberate and seamless:
Email first
– Eliminating the need for a separate guest and owner communication tool.
WhatsApp next
– Centralizing owner and guest messages in a single view.
Phone system transition
– Moving away from legacy providers to unify all support channels.
Live chat integration
– Replacing their previous widget with Conduit for a more direct, streamlined guest experience.
“You guys have absolutely nailed the design—it's the sharpest platform I’ve seen,” Nick said. “What you’ve built is as good as anything we’ve used before, but finally tailored to hospitality.”
The Impact
Since making the switch, Bocobay has seen immediate improvements across their team’s efficiency and guest interactions:
Faster, more consistent messaging
– AI-assisted replies ensure that every guest receives timely, polished responses.
Stronger performance tracking
– Conduit surfaces insights on response times, top-performing agents, and guest satisfaction metrics.
Seamless team collaboration
– Internal teams now rely on Conduit's notes and tagging features to improve handoffs and accountability.
Better owner relations
– Owner communication has been streamlined, reducing back-and-forth across multiple channels.
“Bad products produce bad workflows, and good tools make everything smoother. What you’ve built is as good as Intercom,” said Nick.
Looking Ahead
For Bocobay, technology isn’t just a tool—it’s a pillar of their hospitality experience.
“The biggest barrier to our growth is communication,” Nick said. “Conduit is now at the center of how we scale.”
Their next step? Bringing WhatsApp calls into Conduit, further consolidating guest and owner interactions into a single platform.
By investing in technology built for the specific needs of vacation rental management, Bocobay isn’t just scaling—it’s redefining what luxury guest communication should look like.

ABOUT:
At HomeHop, we curate thoughtfully furnished homes perfect for every kind of traveler —whether you’re here for a few nights, a week, or a few months.
USING CONDUIT SINCE:
June 2025
"The ability to use AI in workflows with SuiteOP is going to be an absolute game changer."
Dan Mitchen
Co-Founder, HomeHop
TL;DR
Grew portfolio from
40 to 108 listings
without hiring additional guest support staff
Achieved
70 percent automation
with a clear path to 24/7 autopilot
Replaced an unreliable VoIP system
and a failed AI vendor with a single unified platform
Zero staff reductions
—VA team shifting from reactive messaging to escalation management
The Challenge
HomeHop nearly tripled its portfolio in two years, from roughly 40 short-term rental listings to 108 across the Cleveland and Akron markets. Messaging volume grew with it, and with it operational challenges.
HomeHop had been burned before. An earlier AI vendor promised to automate guest messaging, but the product never worked as advertised, and support was slow to help.
"It was just issue after issue after issue," Dan said. "It didn't do what they said it was supposed to do. Very, very underwhelming."
Dan lost confidence in AI chatbots and automatic guest messaging. Virtual assistants spent their shifts jumping between Google Drive and communication tools, hunting for the right piece of information before they could reply to a guest.
The phone system compounded the problem. HomeHop relied on Google Voice until the day the team got locked out—no password reset, no support line. They had to rebuild from nothing.
HomeHop had the ambition to scale, but the operations couldn't support it. Every new property meant more messages, more calls, and more pressure on a team already stretched thin. The infrastructure to sustain growth was not there.
The Solution
Dan's business partner Nate pushed to try Conduit despite the previous AI failure.
"I was a little leery, just to be completely honest, just because the whole AI thing didn't work for us before," Dan said. "So why would it now?"
They gave it a chance. Confidence built as the AI responses made sense and the team could control when to approve messages and when to run on autopilot.
HomeHop deployed Conduit across every channel—email, SMS, OTA messaging—so guest inquiries flowed through one system and could be managed by AI. They added voice AI for overnight phone coverage between 1 AM and 7 AM, it replaced the night shift entirely.
The team wired Conduit into the tools they already used. Notion and Slack picked up operational knowledge. SuiteOP handled property operations, linking guest verification and door codes into automated workflows. The team stopped toggling between tabs.
"The way that those two things integrate has just been awesome," Dan said of SuiteOP. "The ability to use AI in workflows with SuiteOP is going to be an absolute game changer."
The Transformation
The AI demanded better inputs. To respond accurately, it needed documented policies, up-to-date property details, and clear procedures. Most of that lived in people's heads, in scattered places, or buried in communication threads. HomeHop focused on formalizing what it knew, and fill in what it didn't.
"By improving the AI, it's forcing us to improve ourselves and improve our processes and improve the quality of the information that we want to give," Abraham said. "You're training someone and then you're like, well, but I don't even have that information. So how am I going to train this one?"
The accuracy work paid off in a second way: it freed the VA team from repetitive messaging. Questions about door codes, parking, check-in instructions, and cancellation policies stopped reaching a human. The team shifted to work that still required judgment—refund requests, emergencies.
The third shift was growth. With guest messaging handled, the team had capacity to onboard new properties properly instead of scrambling to keep up. HomeHop is migrating vendor contacts from Google Sheets into Conduit's maintenance inbox, building a system it can replicate as it enters new markets beyond Cleveland and Akron.
"Whether we're at a hundred units or two hundred units, I don't see us needing to hire additional employees to handle guest messaging," Dan said.
Results
Nearly three times portfolio growth
—from 40 to 108 properties in two years without adding guest support headcount
After-hours AI coverage
from 1 AM to 7 AM across messaging and voice
Replaced Google Voice
with reliable phone and SMS through Conduit
Unified communications
—guest messaging, vendor coordination, and phone in one system
Looking Ahead
Abraham is working with his team through the knowledge base and escalation center, clearing gaps to push automation toward 24/7 autopilot. The team is migrating vendor contacts into Conduit to extend their Cleveland playbook into new markets.
HomeHop operates 108 short-term rental listings across the Cleveland and Akron markets. The company has been a Conduit customer for approximately two years and is currently expanding into additional markets.

ABOUT:
Cosmica operates hospitality brands across Italy and Dubai. Its teams coordinate premium guest services and upsells in Dubai alongside maintenance, cleaning, and field operations in Italy.
USING CONDUIT SINCE:
September 2025 in Dubai and October 2025 in Italy
“If we can reduce the mental workload of the team, then the team can focus on growth.”
Francesco
Founder, Cosmica Group and Mattone.co
About Cosmica
Operating hospitality brands across Italy and Dubai requires balancing two very different business models.
In Dubai, guests often expect premium experiences and personalized services. Upsells such as transportation, activities, early check-ins, and luxury add-ons create meaningful opportunities to increase revenue while enhancing the guest experience.
In Italy, the operational challenge is different. Success depends on coordinating maintenance issues, field teams, cleaners, and property operations efficiently while delivering fast, reliable support to guests.
As Cosmica expanded across both markets, guest communication volume continued to grow. The team found itself spending increasing amounts of time answering repetitive questions, coordinating routine operational tasks, and managing requests that often did not require direct human intervention.
"We used a lot of time answering the same questions and providing the same information over and over again," said Francesco, Founder of Cosmica Group and Mattone.co.
The challenge wasn't simply handling more messages. It was finding a way to grow without continuously adding headcount while still maintaining a high standard of guest service.
The Challenge
Before implementing Conduit, much of the team's day was consumed by repetitive guest communication and operational coordination.
Many of these issues could be resolved quickly if guests had immediate access to the right information, but they still required team members to manually respond and coordinate next steps.
As the company grew, operational complexity was increasing. New bookings, maintenance requests, cleaning coordination, guest arrivals, and vendor communication all needed to happen seamlessly across multiple markets and time zones. Hiring additional virtual assistants seemed like the natural solution; however, Cosmica saw a different opportunity.
Rather than continuing to add layers of support staff, the team wanted to create systems that could handle routine work automatically while allowing employees to focus on higher-value activities.
The Solution
With Conduit, Cosmica centralized guest communication and began automating many of the repetitive workflows that previously required manual effort.
Guests now receive immediate assistance for common questions and troubleshooting requests, significantly reducing the amount of routine work handled by the operations team. For maintenance-related issues, AI-powered responses often help guests resolve problems on their own without requiring a technician or staff member to intervene.
"The satisfaction is higher because guests get a really fast answer. Sometimes they just want to feel that someone is helping them," said Francesco.
Beyond guest messaging, Conduit became an operational platform for the business. The team automated arrival coordination, maintenance workflows, and cleaning notifications that previously required constant manual oversight.
The result was not simply faster responses; it was a shift in how the team spent its time.
A Different Approach to Scaling
One of the most significant outcomes was that Cosmica was able to grow without expanding its support team.
As automation became more capable, the company gradually eliminated its reliance on outsourced virtual assistants. Rather than using automation to replace its core employees, Cosmica used it to invest more deeply in the people already on the team.
The impact was noticeable almost immediately.
With repetitive work removed from their daily responsibilities, team members became more engaged and proactive. Instead of spending their days responding to the same questions repeatedly, they began looking for additional processes that could be automated and improved.
According to the team, the conversation shifted from "How do we keep up?" to "What can we optimize next?"
The remaining team felt more ownership over operations because they were no longer acting primarily as message responders. They became builders, problem solvers, and operators focused on improving the business.
"My internal team is feeling more satisfied because they know they can manage more. They feel that they can grow with the company."
This created a positive feedback loop. As automation reduced workload, the team had more time to improve processes. As processes improved, the business became more efficient. And as the company became more efficient, employees felt increasingly empowered to contribute at a higher level.
This became one of the most valuable benefits of automation: not reducing headcount, but increasing the impact of every person on the team.
Supporting Two Very Different Markets
Conduit also helped Cosmica tailor operations to the unique needs of each market.
In Dubai, automation supports a highly service-oriented guest experience. Guests can easily request additional services, experiences, and upgrades, allowing the company to generate meaningful upsell revenue while delivering a premium hospitality experience.
At peak performance, upsells and cross-sells represented approximately 5% of total revenue in the market.
In Italy, the value comes from operational efficiency. Automating maintenance coordination, guest communication, and property operations allows the team to resolve issues faster and keep properties running smoothly without adding additional operational complexity.
While the business challenges differ between markets, both benefit from the same underlying approach: reducing repetitive work so the team can focus on activities that create greater value for guests and the business.
The Impact
Today, Cosmica manages operations across Italy and Dubai with greater efficiency and flexibility than before.
Guest questions are resolved faster. Operational workflows require less manual coordination. Upsell opportunities are captured more consistently. Most importantly, the team spends less time reacting to repetitive tasks and more time improving the guest experience.
What began as an effort to automate guest communication evolved into something much larger: a more scalable operating model and a more empowered team.
By centralizing communication and automating routine workflows, Cosmica has created a foundation for growth that allows the business to expand across markets while giving its team the tools and confidence to take on bigger challenges.
Looking Ahead
Cosmica continues to expand automation across guest communication, payments, smart lock operations, maintenance coordination, and field service workflows.
As the business grows, the goal remains the same: eliminate repetitive work, empower employees, and allow teams to focus on delivering exceptional hospitality.
For Cosmica, automation is not about replacing people. It's about giving people the ability to do more meaningful work.
"If we can reduce the mental workload of the team, then the team can focus on growth."
Cosmica's ambitions now reach beyond its own portfolio. Through Mattone.co, the property-management academy run by Cosmica Group, the team trains other operators on the same playbook it built for itself, with the guest-messaging AI at the center of that system running on Conduit.
By replacing repetitive tasks with intelligent automation, Cosmica has built a hospitality operation that can scale across markets while keeping its team engaged, motivated, and focused on what matters most.

Every DIY build hits the same three walls

Context
A single guest thread plus their reservation history, your listings, your house rules, and last night's maintenance log blows straight past any prompt window. Conduit pre-computes that context so the agent walks into every conversation already knowing the situation.

Maintenance

Hospitality is all about the experience. We help teams deliver it, better.
Conduit is an AI agent platform purpose-built for hospitality. Hotels, vacation rentals, and resorts build and deploy their own agents to communicate with guests and coordinate the operations behind them.
View open roles
[
1
]
What we believe
01
Experience is the whole business.
Hospitality is 10% of global GDP, and customer experience drives the industry. Better experiences increase satisfaction, sales, and demand, and both the operator and the guest come out ahead.
02
Resolution speed drives the experience.
Guests remember how quickly their needs are met. Resolving requests immediately can turn good service into a great stay.
03
Resolution requires coordination.
In hospitality and in the real world at large, closing one request means moving across several tools and between several people. That coordination is the work.
04
Agents should automate the work.
LLMs gave us the intelligence to go past Q&A: multi-party coordination, upselling workflows that run for days, task management that assigns and tracks real work.

Conduit vs Canary Technologies
Canary Technologies is a strong, broad guest-management suite for hotels: contactless check-in, upsells, digital tipping, guest messaging, AI Voice, and, more recently, an AI Agent Studio. It is a polished, enterprise-grade suite. Conduit is a different kind of thing, and the distinction matters when you are evaluating where AI actually moves the needle.
Conduit is
agentic infrastructure.
You configure a knowledge base and a set of tools, and those drive a customer-facing agent that runs on Conduit's own conversational harness, with guardrailing and reliability built in. That agent does not just answer, it resolves. And it is paired with
Conduit Ops
, an internal operations layer where the same agent dispatches housekeeping and maintenance, manages tasks and supplies, and coordinates door access across systems, the back-of-house work, not just the guest message.
Both have voice and “agents” now. The difference is what happens after the answer.
Canary ships AI Voice and has launched an AI Agent Studio and an Agentic Sales Coordinator, real steps into agent territory. But those are productized flows: templated front-desk, concierge, and reservations agents, plus check-in, upsell, and payment rails, that operate inside Canary's own guest-experience surface. When a request needs work done in your other systems, it routes to staff.
Conduit's agents take the request Canary would escalate and finish it. For an early check-in: the agent checks the PMS, dispatches the turnover through Conduit Ops, charges the fee, processes payment, confirms with the guest, and logs it, in one thread. Same for a 2am checkout extension, an 11pm broken-heater report, a refund. That is multi-step resolution across systems, not a fixed menu of flows.
The real axis of comparison
The useful question is not prebuilt-suite versus build-your-own. Conduit is fully configurable, you are not writing code, you are configuring knowledge and tools, and the agents adapt to your operation and improve over time. The real axis is whether there is an agent underneath that reasons and acts across your whole stack, or a set of purpose-built rails. Canary's suite stacks modules and templated agents for discrete touchpoints; Conduit runs an agent that reasons and acts across them, then does the operational work behind it.
Where Conduit is stronger
Action across your systems.
The agent writes back to the PMS, charges cards, and coordinates your other tools, not just Canary's own check-in and upsell flows.
Conduit Ops.
An internal operations layer, housekeeping, maintenance dispatch, tasks, supplies, door locks, that the agent operates directly. Canary routes operational work to staff.
Conduit Portals.
Generative guest and owner portals with upsells and direct booking, so you match Canary's guest-journey surface and get the action-taking agent behind it.
Chat and voice on one brain.
Configurable, guardrailed, self-correcting agents across chat and voice, sharing the same reasoning and reservation context, rather than separate channel products.
Explainability.
A full reasoning trace: the tools the agent called and the path to each decision, so your team can validate it in production.
Proven and compliant
Conduit runs across 300+ hospitality brands in 120+ countries, has handled 50M+ guest conversations and $3B+ in reservation value, and is SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, GDPR, and ISO 27001 certified. Haven runs 95 percent automation across 270 properties.
Where Canary is a fit
If you primarily want a packaged, enterprise guest-management suite, contactless check-in, digital tipping, upsell modules, with AI layered across them, Canary is a mature, well-supported choice. If a configurable agent that resolves across your systems and an operations layer that does the work are central to your decision, that is where Conduit's agentic infrastructure pulls ahead.

# HostAI becomes Conduit, raises $3.1M

Artificial intelligence-powered short-term rental (STR), hotel and housing platform HostAI has become Conduit and raised $3.1 million.

Cole Rubin, co-founder and CEO of Conduit, shared the news in a lengthy post on LinkedIn and said the seed funding will accelerate growth and enable the company to work with more real estate operators.

Conduit, which started out calling itself “Shopify for Travel,” has grown from an automated guest messaging tool for STRs “into something much bigger,” Rubin said.

“The short-term rental industry pushed us in that direction,” Rubin said. “It was chaotic—operators were juggling dozens of tools, and the integration landscape was nowhere near mature enough to support a viable third-party messaging product—core integrations didn’t exist.”

The company built workarounds in response, integrating with Airbnb’s application programming interface, developing more features, developing more integrations and now working with STR managers around the globe. The efforts laid the groundwork for the company in its new iteration as Conduit, Rubin said.

“Conduit partners with enterprise property managers across all asset classes to power the future of real estate operations—with AI at the core. Real estate is a conversation-driven industry,” Rubin said. “Leasing, retention, maintenance, scheduling—it all runs on messaging and phone calls. But most operators are still stuck with fragmented systems and manual workflows. We saw a better way.”

Conduit’s AI agents can handle voice and text conversations and be integrated with companies’ businesses, from systems to documentation. They’re meant to function like “your best team member,” according to Rubin, who said the agents are responsive, consistent and know when to “escalate.”

Specific capabilities include unit leasing, resolving guest issues, collecting payments and driving renewals.

Rubin said the hope is the agents will serve as a communication engine to improve revenue and conversions and cut operational cost while maintaining quality.

The new funding was led by Pi Labs, according to investor Dhruv Gupta, who also shared the news on LinkedIn.

“We are thrilled to lead the $3.1 million seed round in Conduit (formerly HostAI), with participation from our friends at Y Combinator led by Pete Koomen, a16z Scout, YouTube co-founder Jawed Karim, Snapdocs founder Aaron King and others,” he said.

Gupta said Conduit's founding team, value proposition, customer perception, market opportunity and AI capabilities were among the key reasons why Pi Labs invested in the company.

“We believe AI agents are the future of property management. Conduit's AI, designed specifically for tenant/guest engagement, positions it as a leader in this technological shift,” Gupta said. “They have a strong product roadmap to maintain their competitive edge.”

/   THE MANIFESTO
The future of coordination.
Conduit is the coordination layer for hospitality. It's an agent that works every channel an operator does, from a guest's late-night WhatsApp to the phone ringing at the front desk, and it acts on the business's behalf instead of just shuttling messages between people. It answers the guest directly. When a job needs someone on the ground, it dispatches the contractor and keeps the owner in the loop. It can close a booking or push a refund through without anyone stepping in. All of that works out of the box, because general intelligence is already good enough for the routine work that fills most of a day. The part that makes it yours is everything underneath: how your operation actually runs, and the exceptions only someone inside it would know. The agent picks that up by working alongside your team. Give it long enough and it stops feeling like software and starts to mirror the place itself.
Five thousand years of routing information through people
In 3300 BCE, the temple administrators of Uruk, the first city in recorded history, ran into a problem we'd still recognize: how do you coordinate complex work across people who can't all be in the same room? Their answer was clay tablets. The scribe who kept them became the world's first knowledge worker, someone whose entire job was to hold and relay information too important to leave to memory.
The Romans faced a harder version of it. A Greek phalanx moved as one rigid block, dependent on line of sight and shouted orders, which was fine at small scale and useless the moment things got complex. Rome's answer was hierarchy: eight men under a decanus, those under a centurion, and so on up the chain, so an order never had to travel more than one level to reach anyone. It was a routing protocol built out of people.
Then the telegraph let information move faster than any person could carry it, and that created a new problem. A company now needed some way to act on all of it at scale. Rockefeller's answer was the modern corporation, vertically integrated and run from the top down. Everything since has been a variation on the same theme, whether it's a rigid matrix org or a flat startup that swears off managers entirely. Each one is another attempt to push information and decisions through people more efficiently. None of them touched the real constraint. Information still had to pass through people, and people have limited bandwidth.
AI is the first thing to break the pattern. Strip away the centuries between them and the scribe in Uruk and the manager in a modern org chart turn out to have the same job: hold the context, and carry the decision from whoever has the authority to whoever does the work. Now that job can run on its own. The agent holds the context and routes the decision, and the judgment at the edges stays where it always was, with the people who were always going to make it.
The bottleneck was never speed
Almost everything a hospitality business does runs through a conversation. Revenue gets made in one, whether it's a question about availability or a booking that closes over WhatsApp at midnight. The problems land in the same place. Pick almost any operational function and you'll find it starts with someone sending a message, the refund that needs approving, the guest who's quietly about to walk.
The last thirty years solved the speed problem. Anyone can reach anyone now, instantly, around the clock, and they do. So the bottleneck moved. It's no longer how fast information travels. It's how fast a person can absorb it and act, and there's a hard ceiling on that.
And the channels don't talk to each other. A guest's question sits for hours while a contractor waits on a reply that landed in the wrong inbox. In one Conduit customer's data, median human response time across a single team ranged from 26 minutes to 46 hours. The agent answers in 93 seconds. It gets worse after hours, which is when most guest messages actually arrive, and when the booking tends to go to whoever replies first.
The usual fix is to throw people at it, a VA or a small offshore team parked across all those inboxes, relaying messages between everyone who needs to talk. It doesn't scale. The shifts grind people down, and context leaks out every time a conversation hops from one app to the next. Worse, the business keeps changing under them, so they're never quite trained for the version of it that exists today. The overhead grows in lockstep with the operator. Hiring has never actually solved orchestration. It just adds more people to it.
What Conduit does
Conduit puts a single agent across every channel an operator uses, and it keeps the full context no matter who's on the other end of the thread, a guest one minute, a contractor the next. It acts in real time. Picture a guest messaging at 1am about a leak. The agent answers on the spot and pings the on-call plumber on WhatsApp. It books the visit for 7am, then emails the owner a summary with a comp already drafted for sign-off. The operator wakes up to a six-line digest and one button to press. The night shift ran itself.
The role that disappears is the one in the middle, the person who shuttles information between tools and decides which specialist needs to see what. The specialist at the edge doesn't go anywhere. The plumber still fixes the leak, the front-desk manager still reads the room; their judgment was never the bottleneck. That middle role only existed because information had to pass through a person, and the moment it doesn't, there's nothing left for it to do.
General intelligence handles the routine out of the box. What it can't know on day one is the part specific to you: how you escalate, and the unwritten rules your team falls back on when a call is genuinely hard. That layer gets built over time. You teach some of it directly, and the agent absorbs the rest by watching how your people handle the cases that don't fit the mold. Either way, the result tracks the operator. Tight instincts and clean process give you a system that holds that standard at scale. A sloppy operation gives you a sloppy agent. The agent reflects how the business already runs; it won't fix it for you.
The same capability runs outbound. A booking confirmation kicks off a pre-arrival flow. A guest who went quiet on a quote gets a nudge two days later. None of this is a separate automation bolted on the side; it's the same agent as everything else, now working toward a goal instead of waiting for a message. The conversation stays open as long as it needs to and closes when it's done, and nobody on the operator's side has to track it by hand.
The early signs
We're still early. The clearest evidence isn't in the metrics, it's in what an operator can pull off now that was flatly impossible a year ago. The metrics are real, though. Conduit has handled more than 50M conversations and influenced over $3B in reservation value. The customer base runs past 300 hospitality brands. They operate in more than 120 countries and 140 languages. The agents resolve 87% of guest communications on their own. CSAT sits at 95%, and a first reply lands in under a minute. Industry-wide, the AI automation rate has roughly doubled in nine months, and the operators who moved early are already pulling away from the ones who waited.
We start in hospitality because it's the sharpest version of the problem anywhere. The conversation volume is brutal and the operations are genuinely messy, which is exactly why the payback shows up in weeks instead of quarters. But hospitality is only the entry point. The coordination layer underneath it, an agent sitting at the center of how a business talks and acts for itself, is where every industry eventually lands. Run it forward: no guest left waiting, no contractor sitting on a message nobody saw. Get there, and coordination stops being the quiet tax that every growing business has simply learned to pay.
-Punn and Cole

How Bali Luxury Stays Used AI Automation to Save $22K/Month and Maximize Exit Valuation

ABOUT:
At Bali Luxury Stays, we’re not just managing villas; we’re crafting unforgettable experiences. Our unique approach blends seamless operations with personalized hospitality, ensuring both owners and guests discover a new standard of luxury in Bali.
FOUNDED:
2025
USING CONDUIT SINCE:
December 2024
"I've just got to stop investing in building our own stuff because these guys are going to do it better."
Darren Morgan
Founder, Bali Luxury Stays
TL;DR:
Goal:
Maximize EBITDA multiple ahead of a business sale
Change:
Replaced 11 virtual assistants with Conduit's AI automation platform
Result:
Reduced labor costs by ~$22,000 per month
Growth:
Scaled by 75 units with zero additional headcount
Automation:
Achieved ~80–85% automation rate for guest messaging
The Challenge: Unlocking a Higher Valuation Through AI Automation
Darren, the founder of Easy BnB, had a clear objective: engineer the business to maximize the exit. In the world of property management acquisitions, valuation hinges on an EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization) multiplier. To reach his ideal payout, Darren needed to widen the gap between revenue and operating expenses.
The existing structure made this difficult. The company relied on a team of
fourteen virtual assistants
to maintain 24/7 coverage. While necessary for guest satisfaction, this heavy labor load acted as a drag on margins. Every dollar spent on staffing was a dollar not counted toward the earnings multiple, effectively capping the business's potential valuation.
Operational friction compounded the financial strain. The team struggled with reliability, often secretly juggling second jobs or missing overnight shifts. Furthermore, the sheer volume of routine, low-value inquiries—"fluff" that consumed 80 percent of communication volume—bogged down the staff, making it impossible to scale the portfolio further without adding even more headcount.
Darren realized that to maximize the exit, he needed to fundamentally alter the P&L structure. As he explained, the strategy relied on "two levers that we're able to pull with using AI first": reducing the existing workforce to cut costs, and using that efficiency to "tip in a heap of properties" to drive revenue without the traditional overhead.
The Solution: Pivoting to an AI-First Guest Communication Strategy
Darren was already on the path to automation, attempting to build a proprietary AI tool internally. However, upon seeing the capabilities of
Conduit's AI platform
, he quickly recognized the superiority of purpose-built technology.
"I've just got to stop investing in building our own stuff because these guys are going to do it better."
He halted the in-house development immediately.
The implementation was surprisingly swift, triggered by a crisis that became a forcing function. One Friday night, with a shortage of staff, Darren had to make a binary decision: rely on the few remaining human staff, or push the entire communications load onto the newly integrated AI system.
"Let's just pull the trigger... I feel like we can fix anything that comes up."
The platform was immediately set to handle
100% of messages during the night shift
and up to 85% of messages during the day.
The Transformation: From Responders to Data Curators
The transition proved successful overnight. The staff who remained were not needed to answer the phone—they were needed to make the AI smarter.
The team's role fundamentally shifted from being reactive responders to proactive
data curators
. Their performance was no longer measured by the number of messages they typed, but by how much "ground truth" data they extracted from the properties and fed into the
AI knowledge base
.
This new model yielded two major operational victories:
Reliability:
The AI eliminated human error and inconsistency, successfully fielding between 80 to 85 percent of all messages without supervision.
Increased Revenue:
The AI excelled at upsells, specifically for early check-in and late check-out. It had "no fear of rejection" and asked every single guest for the sale, whereas human staff often hesitated.
The Results: Engineering a Successful Exit with AI
The implementation of the AI automation platform became the core strategy for a successful business exit. By replacing eleven VAs with a single, fixed-cost software subscription, Easy BnB immediately boosted its EBITDA.
Key outcomes:
Metric / Result
Monthly cost savings: ~$22,000
New properties added: 75 units
Additional staff hired: 0
Guest messaging automation: 80-85%
Simultaneously, the platform created a capacity cushion that allowed the business to scale rapidly and safely. In the time leading up to the acquisition, Easy BnB added
seventy-five new properties
to its portfolio without adding a single new full-time employee.
This decoupling of labor and growth was the ultimate win. By increasing the profit and demonstrating superior scalability (a higher number of properties managed per employee), the company was able to command a significantly higher multiple on its valuation.
The Blueprint: AI-First Property Management for the Future
Darren's journey with Easy BnB was so successful that he is replicating the strategy in his new venture, Bali Luxury. Having learned the power of the "AI first" approach, he is building the new company from Day Zero with automation as the foundation.
He is setting up data structures and a knowledge base before hiring the team, ensuring that labor is never the bottleneck to growth.
"We all agree that
AI first is the best approach
."
The success of Easy BnB proved that artificial intelligence is not just a tool for marginal cost savings—it's the single most powerful lever for engineering a high-value, successful business exit in property management.

HostAI becomes Conduit, raises $3.1M
News
/
Startups
By
Morgan Hines
|
April 11, 2025
Share
Artificial intelligence-powered short-term rental (STR), hotel and housing platform HostAI has become
Conduit
and raised $3.1 million.
Cole Rubin, co-founder and CEO of Conduit, shared the news in a lengthy
post on LinkedIn
and said the seed funding will accelerate growth and enable the company to work with more real estate operators.
Conduit, which started
out calling itself “Shopify for Travel,”
has grown from an automated guest messaging tool for STRs “into something much bigger,” Rubin said.
“The short-term rental industry pushed us in that direction,” Rubin said. “It was chaotic—operators were juggling dozens of tools, and the integration landscape was nowhere near mature enough to support a viable third-party messaging product—core integrations didn’t exist.”
The company built workarounds in response, integrating with Airbnb’s application programming interface, developing more features, developing more integrations and now working with STR managers around the globe. The efforts laid the groundwork for the company in its new iteration as Conduit, Rubin said.
“Conduit partners with enterprise property managers across all asset classes to power the future of real estate operations—with AI at the core. Real estate is a conversation-driven industry,” Rubin said. “Leasing, retention, maintenance, scheduling—it all runs on messaging and phone calls. But most operators are still stuck with fragmented systems and manual workflows. We saw a better way.”
Conduit’s AI agents can handle voice and text conversations and be integrated with companies’ businesses, from systems to documentation. They’re meant to function like “your best team member,” according to Rubin, who said the agents are responsive, consistent and know when to “escalate.”

Specific capabilities include unit leasing, resolving guest issues, collecting payments and driving renewals.
Rubin said the hope is the agents will serve as a communication engine to improve revenue and conversions and cut operational cost while maintaining quality.
The new funding was led by Pi Labs, according to investor Dhruv Gupta, who also shared the news
on LinkedIn
.
“We are thrilled to lead the $3.1 million seed round in Conduit (formerly HostAI), with participation from our friends at Y Combinator led by Pete Koomen, a16z Scout, YouTube co-founder Jawed Karim, Snapdocs founder Aaron King and others,” he said.
Gupta said Conduit's founding team, value proposition, customer perception, market opportunity and AI capabilities were among the key reasons why Pi Labs invested in the company.
“We believe AI agents are the future of property management. Conduit's AI, designed specifically for tenant/guest engagement, positions it as a leader in this technological shift,” Gupta said. “They have a strong product roadmap to maintain their competitive edge.”

# Conduit Review: AI Voice Agents for Property Management Operations

Conduit deploys AI voice agents trained on property management workflows with native Yardi and AppFolio integrations. Reviewed by BestCRE using the 9AI Framework.

B

The commercial real estate industry spent an estimated $15.8 billion on property management technology in 2025, according to JLL’s PropTech report, yet tenant communication remains one of the most operationally expensive and inconsistent functions in the stack. CBRE’s 2025 Occupier Survey found that 62 percent of property managers cite after hours service requests as their single largest staffing cost driver, with average response times exceeding four hours for non emergency maintenance calls. Cushman and Wakefield estimates that a typical 500 unit multifamily property fields between 1,200 and 1,800 inbound calls per month, and that roughly 40 percent of those calls are repeat inquiries that could be resolved without human intervention. The gap between tenant expectations and operational capacity is widening as portfolios scale, creating a structural demand for AI systems that can absorb conversational volume without sacrificing service quality.

Conduit, formerly known as HostAI, is a Y Combinator backed AI agent platform that automates customer conversations for property management teams. The platform deploys voice and text AI agents trained specifically on property workflows, capable of triaging maintenance requests, distinguishing emergencies from routine issues, and routing calls to the appropriate resolution path. Conduit integrates natively with Yardi, AppFolio, and Buildium, which allows it to create work orders, update tenant records, and provide real time status updates without manual handoffs. The company raised $3.1 million in seed funding led by Pi Labs with participation from Y Combinator and YouTube co founder Jawed Karim.

Conduit earns a 9AI Score of 87 out of 100, reflecting strong integration depth with major property management systems and a differentiated approach to conversational AI in a sector where automation has historically underperformed. The score is anchored by native workflow connectivity and innovation in voice AI, tempered by early stage market presence and limited published performance benchmarks.

This review is part of BestCRE’s systematic coverage of commercial real estate AI tools across 20 CRE sectors. For the full AI tools directory, see our Best CRE AI Tools hub.

## What Conduit Does and How It Works

Conduit is an AI agent platform that handles inbound and outbound conversations for property management companies through voice calls, SMS, email, and chat. The system is trained on property management workflows rather than general customer service scripts, which means it understands the difference between an emergency water leak that requires immediate escalation and a routine HVAC filter replacement that can be logged as a standard work order. When a tenant calls, the AI agent answers, identifies the nature of the request, creates or updates the appropriate record in the connected property management system, and either resolves the issue autonomously or routes it to the correct human staff member with full context attached.

The platform’s architecture is built around deep integrations with the property management software that operators already use. Native connectors to Yardi, AppFolio, and Buildium mean that Conduit can pull tenant information, property details, and maintenance histories in real time during a conversation. This eliminates the double entry problem that plagues many bolt on communication tools and allows the AI to provide informed responses rather than generic scripts. For example, when a tenant calls about a maintenance issue, Conduit can confirm the unit number, check for open work orders on the same issue, and provide an estimated resolution timeline based on historical data from the property management system.

Conduit’s conversational agents also handle leasing inquiries, tour scheduling, and follow up communications, which extends its value beyond maintenance triage into revenue generating workflows. The platform supports multilingual interactions and can operate around the clock, which addresses the after hours service gap that represents one of the most persistent operational challenges in multifamily and commercial property management. The company positions itself as a replacement for answering services and call centers, with the additional capability of executing actions inside connected systems rather than simply taking messages. For property management companies running portfolios of several hundred to several thousand units, Conduit aims to reduce headcount dependency on repetitive conversational tasks while maintaining or improving tenant satisfaction scores.

### CRE Relevance: 7/10

Conduit was built from the ground up for the property management and housing sector, which gives it a meaningful edge over general purpose conversational AI platforms that require extensive customization to handle real estate workflows. The platform understands lease terminology, maintenance categorization, and the operational rhythms of multifamily and commercial property management. Its origin as HostAI, focused on short term rental management, demonstrates a lineage rooted in real estate operations rather than a pivot from an unrelated industry. The relevance is strongest for multifamily operators, student housing managers, and mixed use property teams that field high volumes of tenant communication. For pure commercial office or industrial portfolios with lower tenant interaction volumes, the value proposition is less pronounced but still applicable for tenant services and building operations. In practice: Conduit addresses a genuine operational pain point in property management that general purpose AI tools have not solved effectively.

### Data Quality and Sources: 5/10

Conduit is a conversational AI platform, not a data analytics or market intelligence tool, which means the data quality dimension is evaluated differently than it would be for a valuation or comp platform. The system does not generate proprietary market data or property level analytics. Instead, its data quality depends on the accuracy of information it pulls from connected property management systems and the reliability of its natural language understanding when processing tenant requests. The platform’s ability to correctly interpret maintenance urgency levels and route calls appropriately is a form of data quality, but it is dependent on the underlying PM system’s data integrity rather than Conduit’s own data assets. The company does not publish accuracy benchmarks for its language understanding or call routing in the way that valuation tools publish error rates. In practice: Conduit’s data handling is functional and context aware, but the platform does not contribute independent data assets to CRE decision making.

### Ease of Adoption: 7/10

The native integrations with Yardi, AppFolio, and Buildium significantly reduce the adoption friction that typically accompanies new technology in property management. Rather than requiring a custom API build or middleware layer, Conduit can connect to the most widely used PM platforms through pre built connectors that sync tenant data, property records, and work order systems. This means a property management company can deploy the platform without a dedicated IT team or extensive configuration work. The setup process involves connecting the PM system, configuring workflow rules for call routing and escalation, and training the AI on property specific information such as amenities, policies, and emergency protocols. Reviews suggest that deployment can be completed within days rather than weeks, which is fast by property management technology standards. The learning curve for staff is minimal because the AI handles the conversations autonomously, with human oversight through a dashboard. In practice: most mid size property management firms can get Conduit operational quickly, though fine tuning escalation rules and exception handling may require ongoing adjustment.

### Output Accuracy: 6/10

Conduit’s output accuracy is measured by how correctly it interprets tenant requests, categorizes issues, and executes the appropriate workflow action. A published case study describes a 500 unit multifamily operator that reduced after hours call escalations by 67 percent using Conduit’s voice AI to triage maintenance requests, automatically create urgent work orders, and provide residents with estimated resolution timelines. That is a meaningful operational result, but the company has not published comprehensive accuracy rates for intent recognition, false positive escalation rates, or tenant satisfaction scores across a broad client base. For a conversational AI system, the risk of inaccuracy includes misclassifying an emergency as routine, failing to capture critical details in a maintenance request, or providing incorrect information about lease terms. The limited volume of published performance data makes it difficult to assess reliability at scale with the same confidence as tools that publish statistical benchmarks. In practice: early results are promising based on available case studies, but the absence of broad published accuracy data warrants conservative scoring.

### Integration and Workflow Fit: 8/10

Integration is Conduit’s strongest dimension. The platform offers native connectors to Yardi, AppFolio, and Buildium, which collectively represent the majority of the property management software market. These are not surface level integrations that simply pass data through an API. Conduit reads from and writes to the PM system in real time, which means it can create work orders, update tenant records, log communication histories, and trigger automated follow ups without requiring manual data entry. This bidirectional integration is critical because it allows the AI agent to function as an extension of the property management system rather than a disconnected communication layer. For property management companies that have standardized on one of these platforms, the integration depth removes a major barrier to adoption. The platform also supports communication channels including voice, SMS, email, and web chat, which consolidates tenant interactions into a single workflow layer. In practice: Conduit’s integration architecture is among the strongest in the CRE conversational AI space and is a primary driver of its value proposition.

### Pricing Transparency: 5/10

Conduit uses a credit based pricing model with tiered plans, but the company does not publish detailed pricing on its website. Third party sources reference a range of approximately $200 to $600 per month for AI powered property management communication platforms, though the exact pricing for Conduit depends on portfolio size, call volume, and the number of integrated properties. The absence of a public pricing page means that prospective customers must engage with sales to get a quote, which is common for enterprise focused property technology but creates friction for smaller operators who want to evaluate cost before committing to a demo. The credit based model adds a layer of complexity because it requires buyers to estimate their usage patterns before they can calculate total cost of ownership. For mid size property management firms budgeting for AI adoption, the lack of published pricing makes it harder to compare Conduit against alternatives without entering a sales process. In practice: pricing information is available through direct engagement but not transparent enough for self serve evaluation.

### Support and Reliability: 5/10

A boutique hotel upsold me before I ever set foot in the building.

24 hours before check-in, instead of the usual "Dear guest, your check-in instructions are attached" email, they texted me a link.

I opened it on my phone: directions from the airport, my room details, the wifi password. While I was poking around, an early check-in and a massage showed up on the front page, and I bought them with Apple Pay, all before I left for my flight.

Then, the moment I landed, I received another text: "Hi Punn, we have a discounted upgrade on the Corner King room you stayed in last time. Let me know if you'd like it. The offer's also in your portal." I thought about it for a second and went for the upgrade.

That hotel made more money off my stay before I walked in, and I had an incredible experience. Because it was so personalized and timely, it never felt like a pitch. It felt like a personal concierge at a hotel who already knew what I liked and exactly when to reach out.

There's demand buried in millions of guest conversations every day. Almost none of it gets captured, because until now it hasn't been practical to.

That's why we built Portals.

It's a single link for the entire stay: instructions, directions, wifi details, digital room keys, in-room controls, an agent that answers anything, and upsell offers personalized to every guest.

Your agents personalize each portal in the conversation and place the most relevant offers at the top. Guests pay in a double-tap with Apple Pay, Google Pay, Link, and more.

Portals is live in Conduit today. Really proud of the team for building a best-in-class product yet again.

src_c46058d8e942af9e.title: Ad Details | LinkedIn
src_c46058d8e942af9e.text:
Cole Rubin

Promoted by Conduit

Every guidebook, welcome book and QR code on the fridge fixes the half of the problem that was never broken.

The pitch makes sense. Guests have questions, so give them a well-organized place to find the answers. Nicer layout, better categories, a link in the pre-arrival message.

We measured whether any of it lands. In threads where the operator had already sent the door code unprompted, before the guest asked anything, 27.4% of guests asked for it regardless. Check-in time ran 20.8%, wifi 18.4%.

That is information sitting on their phone, in a thread they already have open. If it gets missed there, a PDF will not rescue it.

Most guidebooks are organized fine. The timing is what fails. The information arrives days before anyone wants it, and when they finally do want it, finding it becomes the guest's job.

So we built the other half. Portals is our guest portal, and the AI chat lives in it. The guest asks the question the way they would say it out loud and gets an answer that knows which property they are standing in.

"What's a good dinner spot for us tonight around here."

Keep the guidebook. Just stop expecting it to answer anything.

Link in the comments.

Overview
Conduit gives your team one workspace for customer conversations, AI agents, workflow automation, and operational records. Start by setting up the workspace and channels, then build the V3 agent surfaces that control what the AI knows, how it behaves, and what actions it can take.
Create workspace
Invite teammates, configure roles, and set the workspace basics.
Connect channels
Bring email, WhatsApp, phone, SMS, widget, and other channels into Conduit.
Build agents
Configure external, internal, and voice agents from the V3 Agents area.
​
Set Up The Workspace
Everything in Conduit happens in your team’s workspace. A workspace contains your members, inboxes, connected channels, Knowledge Base, agents, tools, workflows, records, and settings.
Workspace setup
Configure the workspace, invite teammates, and decide who can manage agent settings.
Inbox and fields
Organize conversations by inbox, contact type, routing, and custom fields.

.

Connect Channels And Integrations
Connect your communication channels to centralize all customer interactions in one place.
Email

WhatsApp Business

Chat Widget

Connect business systems and data sources after your channels are working.
PMS and integrations

Marketplace
Install apps, agent templates, skill templates, and workflow templates.
​
Build The V3 Agent System
V3 separates the agent system into focused surfaces. Use each one for the right kind of configuration.
Agents
Create customer, internal, and voice agents, then configure persona, behavior, triggers, and publish state.
Knowledge
Add pages, folders, documents, links, and synced data sources that agents can retrieve as facts.
Skills
Write reusable instructions that combine policy, process, variables, and tool-use guidance.
Tools
Enable connection tools, custom Python or JavaScript tools, MCP tools, and per-agent overrides.

Test And Deploy

Operator

Sandbox testing
Test a specific agent with realistic customer, listing, and reservation context.
Road to Autopilot

V3 migration

Using the Inbox
A clean inbox is still the daily operating surface. Conversations flow through Todo, Follow-Up, and Done, while agent activity, sources, and tool calls give your team visibility into how each response was produced.

3.15
SEPTEMBER 18, 2026
Major Features
Custom workspace roles
Build your own roles instead of choosing only Admin or Member. Create a role, pick exactly which pages and actions it can reach, and assign it to teammates or pending invites. Built-in roles stay put, and a role that is currently assigned to someone is protected from accidental deletion.
Find it under Settings → Members → Roles and permissions.
Enhanced Capabilities
Attach files to workflow messages
Workflow "Send message" steps can now carry file attachments, including files pulled from workflow variables. Send documents, guides, and forms automatically as part of an automation instead of pasting links.
Find it under Workflows → open a workflow → a Send message step.
More ways to filter your inbox
Quick filters in the inbox sidebar now include the same custom fields, listings, and assignee options as the full filter menu, and you can save them as views. Slice your conversations the way your team actually works.
Find it under Inbox → Filters.
Set your own warm-transfer wait time
Voice agents that warm-transfer a call to a person can now use a wait time you configure, so the hand-off matches how quickly your team picks up instead of a fixed default.
Find it under AI Agents → Voice → Escalations.
Target guest verification by custom attributes
Guest verification rules can now be scoped by the custom attributes on a reservation, so you can require the right checks for the right stays instead of applying one blanket rule.
Find it under Portals → Verification.
Pause and reactivate a reservation's guest portal
Turn an individual reservation's guest portal off and back on without deleting anything. Useful when a stay is on hold or a guest shouldn't have portal access for a while.
Find it under a reservation's detail panel → Portal.
One-click reconnect for PMS connections
Each PMS connection on the settings page now has its own Reconnect button that repairs that exact integration, instead of adding a new connection row. Reconnecting a property is now unambiguous.
Find it under Settings → Connections → PMS.
Configure how tasks are marked done
Choose which status counts as "done" per task category and control task completion behavior, so your operations board reflects your own workflow.
Find it under Settings → Operations → Task statuses.
Performance & Quality Improvements
Workflows
: Workflow steps now show template names and their approval status, so it's clear which message template a step will send.
Translation
: Added Polish for chat translation and AI agents.
Chat widget
: Polished interactions, layout, and scrolling in the chat widget.
Voice
: Corrected the message shown when a call is canceled before it's answered.

3.14
SEPTEMBER 11, 2026
Major Features
Security deposits in guest portals
Collect, hold, and release security deposits right through your guest portals. Guests see the deposit amount and its status before they check out, holds are captured or released as the stay progresses, and every deposit keeps a full history you can review and act on.
Find it under Portals → Transactions → Security deposits.
Enhanced Capabilities
Change door codes without leaving the inbox
Set, update, and retry a reservation's smart-lock door code straight from the inbox, and mark access codes and portals active or inactive as availability changes. Access codes can also be updated programmatically through the API.
Find it in the inbox reservation panel, or under Devices.
Turn any message into a task
Create a task directly from a guest message — the details are drafted for you from the conversation — through a redesigned new-task modal.
Find it in the inbox: open a message and choose Create task, or start one under Operations → Tasks.
Speaker labels in call summaries
Call summaries now identify who said what, so agent and guest turns are clear at a glance.
Find it in a call's summary in the inbox.
Video walkthroughs in listing details
Video links you add to a listing now render as rich preview cards in the guest-facing listing details, instead of a plain URL.
Find it under Portals → Listing details → open a listing.
Clearer workforce call reporting
Workforce now separates abandoned calls, where the caller hung up, from missed calls, with a dedicated abandoned-call-rate metric. Live and Overview also show real-time ticket counts with per-inbox and per-call-group breakdowns.
Find it in the org dashboard under Workforce → Misses and Overview.
Verification rules by booking date
Portal verification rules can now be scoped to a booking's dates, so ID and document checks apply only to the stays you choose.
Find it under Portals → Verification.
Performance & Quality Improvements
New widget chats start fresh instead of resurfacing a previous session.
Chat tool cards stay in place after a reply finishes, with smoother transitions in the chat widget.
Conduit no longer answers a call the caller has already hung up on.
Insights dashboards now load reliably across month-long date ranges.
Opening a workflow now takes you straight to its latest draft.
Guest PDFs now render emoji and international characters correctly.

3.13
SEPTEMBER 4, 2026
Major Features
Guest portals for every reservation
Generate a guest portal straight from a reservation. Open a reservation, and if it doesn't have a portal yet, create one in a click from the sidebar, scoped to that exact stay. A new workflow trigger fires the moment a guest finishes portal check-in, so the rest of your arrival flow can run on its own.
Find it under Reservations, open a reservation, and use the portal panel in the sidebar. The trigger is in the workflow builder as "Portal check-in completed."
Run your connected apps inside workflows
A workflow step can now run the tools from apps you've connected, like Monday.com or Asana, as a Run Tool step. Pass in parameters, including lists and structured values, and if a tool fails you get the real reason back instead of a generic error. Managers can refresh a connection's tool list so newly available tools show up without reconnecting.
Find it in the workflow builder: add a Run Tool step and pick a connected app's tool.
Enhanced Capabilities
See guest ID and selfie when you review check-in
When you review a guest's identity verification, you now see the ID front and back and the liveness selfie right in the review panel, so you can approve or reject without leaving Conduit.
Find it where you review check-in verification submissions.
Route each task category to its own Slack channel
Choose which Slack channel every task category posts to, so the right team sees the right work. You can also require specific custom fields before a task in a category can be marked complete.
Find it under Operations, then Tasks, in category settings.
Plan the day in Operations
Clearer day planning on the operations schedule, a new Trips table, and a "no assignee" filter to find unassigned tasks fast.
Find it under Operations, in Schedule and Tasks.
A contact's tasks, right in the inbox
Open a conversation and see every task tied to that contact in a new Tasks tab, without switching pages.
Find it in the Inbox conversation sidebar.
WhatsApp calls follow your call groups
Inbound WhatsApp calls now route through your call groups, ringing the right people and rolling to voicemail on the same rules as your phone lines.
Find it under Settings, then Call groups.
The chat widget remembers recent conversations
Guests returning to your website widget can pick up recent conversations again instead of starting over.
Find it in the chat widget on your website.
Search and filter workflow runs
Find a specific workflow run fast with new search and filters, and page through long histories without losing your place.
Find it under Workflows.
Keypad and access codes
Add a submit key to keypad access codes, and generate a guest's door code from the phone number on their reservation.
Find it under Devices.
Voice callbacks
When a caller asks for a callback, the voice agent can capture it as a note so your team can follow up.
Search reservations by confirmation ID
Search the inbox for a reservation by its PMS online confirmation ID.
Find it in the Inbox search bar.
Portal improvements
Group your upsell offers into categories guests browse in the portal
Embed YouTube videos in listing details
Let guests decline a damage waiver or security deposit when you allow it
Guest contact details from the portal now sync into your Conduit contacts
Show a notice in the portal when a guest's request has been escalated
Override the map link shown for a listing
Performance & Quality Improvements
Calls
: A refused call retries on a fresh device instead of dropping
Calls
: Stopped sending callers to voicemail after their agent had already joined
WhatsApp setup
: Clear guidance when your WhatsApp Business account doesn't match
Help
: Fixed broken in-app help links
Calendar
: Polished date-range calendar styling and filter controls

3.12
AUGUST 28, 2026
Major Features
Jobber integration
Connect your Jobber account to Conduit. Jobber's jobs and work orders are now available as tools your AI agents and the public API can use, and a Jobber job change can trigger a workflow. Set up automations that fire when a job is scheduled, updated, or completed.
Find it in the workflow builder: add a trigger and pick Jobber. Jobber's work-order tools are also available to your AI agents and through the public API.
Book directly in the chat widget
The chat widget can now walk a guest through a booking without leaving the conversation: browse a listing, check availability, choose the guest count, and get a checkout link, all inline. It works across your connected property systems.
Find it in the chat widget on your website.
Enhanced Capabilities
Noise cancellation on calls
Turn on background noise cancellation so voices come through clearly on noisy lines.
Find it under the call panel's audio settings.
Search inside attachments
Inbox and ticket search now looks inside attachments, so you can find a conversation by the contents of a file someone sent, across every channel.
Find it in the Inbox search bar.
Post task activity to Slack
Task updates can now flow into a Slack thread, so the right people stay in the loop without opening Conduit. You can also update tasks, including custom fields, straight from the AI operator.
Find it under Operations → Tasks, and connect Slack under Settings → Connections.
Pause a contact's AI over the API
The public API can now pause and resume AI replies for a specific contact, so your own tools can hand a conversation to a human and take it back.
Find it in the public API reference.
Give workflow AI steps their own tools
When an AI step sends a message in a workflow, you can now grant it specific tools to use, so it can look things up or take action mid-workflow.
Find it in the workflow builder on the Send AI Message step.
Door codes in the inbox before check-in
Access codes now show in the conversation sidebar before a stay is activated, so you can share them without digging.
Find it in the Inbox conversation sidebar.
File uploads in Portal questions
Guide portals can now ask a guest to upload a file as an answer (an ID photo, a signed form), and it appears with the submission.
Find it under Portals when editing additional questions; uploads show with each submission.
Chat widget: pets and returning guests
The widget's guest count picker now includes pets, and returning visitors skip the intro setup and go straight to chatting.
Find it under Settings → Channels → Widget.
New property system: Avantio
Avantio is now available as a property management connection.
Find it under Settings → Connections when adding a property system.
Guest portal in the guest's language
Guests can now translate their guide portal into their own language with one tap, so check-in steps, house guides, and offers read clearly no matter where they are from.
Find it in the guest portal, where guests get a language picker that translates the content.
Performance & Quality Improvements
Workflow builder
: nested branch conditions render correctly, branch sheets open in place, and stale canvas state no longer blocks the AI operator. Note mentions render as written.
Calls
: audio devices wait for setup before going live; voicemail timeout fixed for simultaneous ringing.
Chat
: rich cards wait for the reply to finish before appearing.
Reporting
: Manager Dashboard filters now apply, and average talk time by workspace was added.
Skills
: recently edited skills sort first, with active-status sorting.
Sandbox
: filter activity to sandbox test runs.
Integrations
: Breezeway now surfaces the real connection error instead of a generic failure; Resly cleaning status syncs automatically as listings change.
Listings settings
: see billable sub-listings and unit totals.
Knowledge base import
: column mapping leads with matched entities and lets you pick the mode.
Scrollbars
: visible and easier to grab across the app.
Operator
: timestamps show in your workspace timezone.
Portals
: ad offers show in discover, and single-guide categories get a full-width tile.
Guide sheets
: capped width and image crop on desktop.
