3.11
AUGUST 21, 2026
Big week for Portals and the chat widget. Stay portals can now time exactly what guests see, the widget has a new Glass look, and Mr Alfred joins the list of supported property management systems.
Major Features
Control what your portal reveals, and when
Time-gate what a stay portal shows guests. Keep arrival details (door codes, address, directions) hidden until a set window before check-in, set field-level visibility for listing details, and give guides their own visibility rules. The portal auto-refreshes to unlock content on schedule, so guests see the right thing at the right time.
Find it under Portals → Settings → Defaults → Visibility timing.
A new Glass theme for the chat widget
The embeddable chat widget gets a translucent Glass appearance, plus left/center/right positioning and light/dark/auto modes, all with a live preview as you configure it. Classic stays the default, so nothing changes unless you want it to.
Find it under Settings → Channels → Widget → appearance.
Mr Alfred PMS integration
Connect Mr Alfred to sync your properties and reservations into Conduit. Set it up from the property-management-system connection list. Sync-only for now: properties and reservations flow in, with two-way guest messaging to follow.
Find it in the PMS connection list when you connect a property management system.
Enhanced Capabilities
Booking notifications for Calendly
When a Calendly booking is created, rescheduled, or canceled, Conduit can email the people you choose. Turn it on and set the recipient list per connection.
Find it under Settings → Connections → Calendly.
Per-listing experience recommendations
Curate which experiences the AI recommends for each individual listing instead of a single account-wide set, so guests get suggestions that fit the property they actually booked.
Find it under Portals → Listing details → Experiences.
Guide categories
Organize your portal stay guides into categories you name, reorder, and manage. Guests see guides grouped by category in the portal instead of one long list.
Find it under Portals → Guides.
Rename your portal's section headers
Rename the guest portal's section headings (Before you arrive, Details, Guides, Discover, and the rest). Leave a field blank to fall back to the default.
Find it under Portals → open a portal → Config → Design.
Import multi-table Notion databases
Notion databases that hold multiple tables can now be imported into the knowledge base. Each table shows up individually in the picker, so you can bring in exactly the ones you want.
Find it under Knowledge Base → Sources → Add source → Notion.
Workspace-branded notification emails
Notification emails now carry your workspace's own name and logo instead of the parent organization's, so recipients see the right brand.
Find it in Workspace settings — your workspace name and logo drive it automatically.
See your cost per credit
The billing page now shows your current cost per credit right in the plan summary.
Find it under Settings → Billing.
Per-channel agent settings for the widget
Tune how a chat agent runs on the website widget separately from your other channels, so you can trade extra processing for faster widget replies.
Find it under AI Agents → a chat agent → Settings.
Organize workflows into folders
A new API to create workflow folders and move workflows between them, with public API-reference docs.
Find it in the API Reference under Workflows.
Performance & Quality Improvements
Portal listings filter
: filter the Portals Listings table by active or inactive, defaulting to active so retired units stay out of the way.
Shareable Offers tab
: the portal Offers tab now has its own link and proper back-button behavior between Stay and Offers.
Portal links in more workflows
: the portal-link variable resolves from the contact when there's no exact reservation, and now appears while you're still drafting a workflow step.
Inbox send
: sending is no longer blocked after the inbox rejects one attachment in a batch. The rejected file is skipped and the rest go through.
Call recordings on hold
: recording now pauses while a caller is on hold, so hold music isn't captured.
Transferred calls
: the call view now shows the original caller's name on directly transferred calls.
Call groups
: the member picker stays open so you can add several members without reopening it.
Operator shortcut
: the keyboard approval shortcut (Cmd/Ctrl+Enter) now works on the full-page Operator, not just the sidebar.
Workflow times
: reservation time variables now render a proper 12-hour clock.
Portal mobile signing
: guest signing sheets stay above the mobile keyboard instead of being covered by it.
Portal images
: images inside an open portal detail sheet load immediately, fixing scroll stalls.
Portal preview
: the config Preview renders the Stay tab even when no check-in step is configured.
Guide editor
: guide settings are grouped into collapsible rows with at-a-glance summaries, and categories reorder by drag.

3.10
AUGUST 14, 2026
Major Features
Configurable offers with variants
Build upsell offers with option groups and variants (sizes, add-ons, and choices) that guests configure themselves right in the portal. Instead of one flat offer, you can now model real products with per-variant pricing, so guests pick exactly what they want and you capture the upsell without a back-and-forth.
Find it under Portals → Offers.
Enhanced Capabilities
Rich text and photos in portal listing details
Listing detail fields now support rich text formatting and inline photos, so the stay page you show guests can be properly formatted with images instead of plain text.
Find it under Portals → Listing details.
Repeatable check-in verification steps
Check-in verification steps can now repeat and stack, so guests complete every required check (multiple IDs, multiple guests, multiple documents) instead of being capped at one.
Find it under Portals → Verification.
A real editor for verification choice questions
Verification choice questions get a proper option editor: add options, drag to reorder, and paste several at once instead of wrestling with a single textarea.
Find it under Portals → Verification.
Redesigned Devices pages
The Devices pages have been rebuilt with grouped device cards, status and battery badges, filters that persist in the URL, and per-device activity. Activity feeds now load automatically as you scroll instead of a "Load more" button.
Find it under Devices.
Ring and voicemail timing for call groups
Set how long each call-group member rings and when an unanswered call rolls to voicemail, so inbound calls follow the escalation path you actually want.
Find it under Settings → Call groups.
KrossBooking status mapping
Map your KrossBooking status codes per account so online check-in completion (and the door-code release that follows) is accurate, and apply a saved mapping to existing upcoming bookings with a preview of what changes before you commit.
Find it under Settings → Connections.
Choose which columns import into the Knowledge Base
When importing a spreadsheet or database into the Knowledge Base, pick exactly which columns get pulled in. New or renamed columns stay excluded until you select them, so an upstream change never quietly reshapes your knowledge base. You can also resume a parked split-by-listing import straight from its source row.
Find it under Knowledge Base → Sources when importing.
Sort the workspace switcher
Sort the workspace switcher by inbox count or by oldest pending message, so the workspaces that need attention rise to the top.
Find it in the workspace switcher at the top of the sidebar.
Per-unit info in workflows
Workflows can now read the specific booked sub-unit on multi-unit properties, so per-unit details (door codes, directions, Wi-Fi) reach the right guest automatically.
Find it in any workflow's variable picker.
Filter reservations by departure date
The reservations API can now be filtered by departure date, making it simple to pull everyone checking out on a given day.
Available on the reservations API.
More AI model choices for the Operator assistant
Two additional AI models are now selectable for the Operator assistant, giving you more control over how it responds.
Find it in the Operator assistant's settings.
Performance & Quality Improvements
Messaging & inbox
New-reservation messages get answered
: guest messages that arrived alongside a brand-new reservation could sit unanswered; the AI now replies.
Conversations close at the right time
: conversations now auto-close only when the AI actually signals it's done.
Cleaner AI messages
: removed a broken "references" tag on AI-sent messages that couldn't be opened.
Channels & PMS
Airbnb request cards show sooner
: modification and booking-request approve/decline cards now appear in the sidebar even before the reservation finishes syncing.
Hostfully images render as images
: image attachments from Hostfully now show inline in the inbox instead of generic download links.
Guest profile links work on Guesty
: guest profile links now open correctly on Guesty workspaces instead of returning a not-found error.
Bookings appear when enabled
: the Bookings nav and inbox Bookings tab now show up for workspaces whose booking tools are turned on.
Knowledge Base & AI
Large portfolios sync
: knowledge syncs now complete smoothly for property portfolios with thousands of listings.
Sources stay organized
: knowledge base sources always stay filed under the connection that imported them, and an import that can't be linked to a live connection now fails with a clear reconnect prompt instead of creating an unmanageable source.
Portals
Portal sheets always render
: guest portal sheets no longer open to an empty surface.
Reliable transaction analytics
: portal transaction analytics now load reliably for high-volume workspaces.
Calls
Voice call step remembers its setup
: the voice-agent call workflow step now reloads its saved phone number and agent when reopened.

3.9
AUGUST 7, 2026
Portal signing gets a big upgrade this week: upload and sign your own PDF agreements. There's a new RapidEye video-inspection integration for field teams, call routing visibility on the phone page, and a new workflow step for reservation fields. Plus a lot of PMS, inbox, and messaging reliability work under the hood.
Major Features
RapidEye video inspections
Connect RapidEye to request and review video property inspections without leaving Conduit. Kick off an inspection from any task and watch it move from recording to processing to completed, right there on the task. A new connect dialog gets you set up in a couple of clicks.
Find it under Settings → Connections to connect, then request an inspection from any task.
Upload and sign your own PDF agreements in portals
Portal signing now handles PDFs, not just rich-text agreements. Upload your own agreement, drop signature and text fields exactly where you want them with a full-screen field mapper, and guests sign it during check-in. Rich-text and PDF signing now run through one unified flow, so every agreement lives in the same place.
Find it under Portals → Verification.
Enhanced Capabilities
Call routing visibility on the phone page
The phone page now shows how each call was routed: which team members it rang and why it went unanswered. It works even for missed calls that never recorded a final outcome, so you can always see what happened.
Find it under Phone.
A workflow step for reservation fields
Add a step to any workflow that updates a reservation's custom field. Portal link variables inside these steps now resolve to real URLs, so you can drop a guest's portal link straight into a reservation field.
Find it in the workflow builder's step picker.
Workflows can check delivery status
Workflow steps can now branch on whether a message was actually delivered (SMS, WhatsApp, or email) before moving on, so you can retry, escalate, or send a fallback when a message doesn't land.
Find it when adding variables to a workflow step.
See existing lock codes, and why a code failed
When you connect a smart-lock account, Conduit now shows the codes already programmed on the lock by a previous system, so nothing is a mystery when you migrate. And when a code fails to program, you get the actual reason (like a full lock) instead of just "Failed".
Find it under Devices.
Voice agents can take a message
Voice agents now have a proper "take a message" action that logs the caller's message as an internal note for your team, instead of accidentally texting or emailing the handoff note back to the caller.
The message shows up as an internal note on the conversation.
Richer listing knowledge from your PMS
Two additions to imported listing knowledge: per-room bed layouts, so your AI can answer which room has which bed, and full check-out details (time, place, and instructions) so it can walk guests through leaving.
It shows up automatically in your AI's answers.
Reservation type as a reservation field
The reservation type from Track now comes in as a reservation custom field, so you can use it in workflows and labels like any other field.
It shows up on the reservation.
Reference reservation statuses in agent instructions
Mention reservation statuses (like Pending Host) directly in agent instructions and skills, the same way you already reference other entities. No more spelling out status names by hand.
Find it when writing agent instructions or skills.
Operations, streamlined into Tasks
The Operations area is now focused on Tasks. Insights and Vendors were taken out of the left navigation, the side menu became section tabs to give the task list more room, and the nav item is now simply labeled Tasks.
Find it under Tasks.
Create or join an organization from settings
The new settings page now lets you create an organization or add your workspace to an existing one, right where the rest of your workspace settings live.
Find it under Settings → General.
Emergency calling from AU, NZ, and UK numbers
Emergency numbers (000, 111, and 999) can now be dialed from Australian, New Zealand, and UK phone numbers.
Find it in the call widget.
Dark mode across the guest portal
The guest-facing portal now has a dark theme. Choose light or dark per portal in your branding settings, and guests see it in the theme you set.
Find it under Portals → your portal → branding.
Vrbo inquiries for every workspace
Vrbo inquiry handling is now on for everyone, so pre-booking questions from Vrbo land in your inbox and get answered like any other channel.
Find it in the Inbox.
Performance & Quality Improvements
Inbox
: Restored Airbnb conversation links, including for reservations without a listing.
Inbox
: Messages sent from your PMS now show a readable provider name instead of appearing blank.
Inbox
: The drafts badge no longer counts drafts left on deleted contacts, and moving between contacts recovers cleanly from stale pagination.
Connections
: Workspace admins can now turn connection tools on and off, not just the person who set up the connection.
Calls
: Missed group-call notifications now go only to the members whose phones actually rang.
Email
: The AI no longer replies to email bounce notifications; a bounce surfaces to a human as a ticket instead.
Email
: Restored replying to guests through Expedia proxy email addresses.
Email
: The connect-a-domain option stays available even when you only have a Gmail account connected.
PMS
: Krossbooking reservation sync now handles large batches reliably.
Availability
: Switching everyone active or away no longer erases your custom per-workspace availability layout.
AI
: Property answers now ground listing names, addresses, and amenities in your connected PMS data for better accuracy.
AI
: Availability answers now include the minimum-stay length and keep the requested listing consistent with any alternatives offered.
Agents
: AI-created tasks now get a due date and a checklist when the work has multiple steps.
Agents
: Restoring an older agent version keeps its tool and listing references working.
Onboarding
: Onboarding now always creates a guest agent, so new workspaces are ready for guest messages from day one.
Portals
: Choosing a damage-waiver or deposit option now opens the next step, the listing picker loads every listing, and dismissing the opportunity pop-up sticks per user.
Integrations
: HOPR room tasks default to the room location, and cancellations are double-checked when the provider returns an ambiguous result.

3.8
JULY 31, 2026
Guest Portals launched last week. This week is all about making them do more: a full digital guidebook, in-portal rental agreement signing, local experiences for guests, and a much smarter offers engine. Plus fixes across calls, the inbox, and PMS syncing.
Major Features
Guest guides — a digital guidebook in every portal
Build a proper guidebook for each stay: house manual, wifi, check-in steps, local tips, directions, whatever your guests need. A block editor lets you lay out sections with a live preview, and guests read it right inside their portal. No more PDFs or copy-pasting the same instructions into every thread.
Find it under Portals → Guides.
Enhanced Capabilities
Sign the rental agreement during check-in
Guests can now draw and sign your rental agreement as part of portal check-in, right on their phone. Each signature is captured with the signer's IP and a timestamp, so you have a clean record of who agreed to what and when.
Find it in Portals → your portal → Check-in.
Show guests things to do with Discover

JUNE 4, 2026
Conduit V3 just went live, with smarter agents, a faster inbox, improved escalations, and Operator. This is the biggest release we have shipped: the whole product is now organized around agents, your agents are split into the ones that talk to your contacts and the ones that run your operations, and every agent has its own home. And Operator, our agentic copilot, is here to do the work you ask of it.
Agents
Your agents now come in two kinds, and the difference is simple. External agents are the ones your contacts talk to. They handle the people writing in, and each one is triggered by an inbox. Internal agents run your operations. They have no inbox, and you trigger them through the channels you set up or by asking Operator.
A page for every agent
Open any agent and you land on its own page. You can see how it has been running at a glance, tune how it behaves, set its personalization and guardrails, and connect it to Slack, all in one place. No more hunting through settings to find one agent's configuration.
Triggers, front and center
The agent sidebar is built around triggers now. External agents live under an inbox trigger. Internal agents live under channel triggers, with Slack available today and Phone, Email, WhatsApp, and Teams on the way.
A marketplace to start from
The new Marketplace gives you a library of ready-made agents and skills. Pick one, install it, and you start from a working setup instead of a blank page. Each one tells you what it needs before it goes live, so there are no surprises.
Inbox
Call straight from a conversation
You can now place a call right from a conversation in the inbox. An inbound text or email can become a live call without you ever leaving the thread.
A calmer way to handle calls
Inbound calls got a real cleanup. A ringing call shows a clear Answer card instead of a pill you might tap by accident, and the call widget collapses to a safe state so nobody joins a call by mistake. If you are marked Away, calls stop ringing you, so they only reach people who can actually pick up.
Less setup, more context
Phone fields default to your workspace's country and preferred number, so you stop re-picking the same sender every time. And the conversation list now shows the booking channel, reservation dates, and status inline, so you can read the state of a booking without opening it.
Escalations
The right issue gets to the right place
When you hand an escalation to Operator, it routes the issue where it belongs and turns down anything it cannot actually act on, instead of quietly doing the wrong thing. And conversations that need a follow-up get put back in the queue, so a contact who needs a second touch is not forgotten.
Operator
Operator is the copilot you talk to, and it does the work. Ask it a question and it answers. Ask it for a report and it builds one. Hand it a pile of work and it triages it. It lives in your sidebar, and you can reach it through Slack too.
Here is some of what Operator can do for you:
Build a polished PDF report from your data, with charts included, ready to download and share.
Export your analytics to a CSV you can open in a spreadsheet.
Answer questions about your numbers and pull insights on demand.
Add contacts and fill in their custom fields.
Update your knowledge base, your agent instructions, and your guardrails.
Set up workflows.
Resolve escalations.
You describe what you need in plain language. Operator figures out the rest, shows its work, and hands you something you can use.

Your customers and teams already live in Slack. Now your AI agents do too.  Connect any Slack channel to Conduit and incoming messages are automatically routed to your inbox with full AI response support. Your agents can read, reply, and resolve conversations  in Slack channels just like they do across email, SMS, and WhatsApp. File attachments, sender identification, and routing rules all work out of the box. You can  also trigger workflows from Slack messages.
WhatsApp Template Rotation
Sending bulk WhatsApp messages at scale? Conduit now automatically rotates across your approved templates in scheduled workflows to avoid Meta rate limits and account flags. If a template or account gets paused, the schedule pauses automatically and resumes when the pause lifts.

Enhanced Capabilities
Widget Customization & Call Transfers
Three improvements to give you more control over the widget experience. Each route option can now display its own custom post-form message, so users see confirmation text tailored to what they selected. Links inside the widget automatically append collected form data and UTM parameters — no manual URL building needed. And call transfers now show clear "Transfer Succeeded" or "Transfer Failed" status pills instead of a generic badge, so your team can see outcomes at a glance.
Faster New Conversation Flow
Starting a new conversation in the widget now takes you straight to the chat view with an instant greeting message, instead of showing a loading screen while things spin up.
Opera HMS Listing Enrichment
Opera-connected listings are now automatically enriched with room types, amenities, restaurants, attractions, transportation, and directions — giving your AI agents much richer context for answering property-specific questions.
Escalation Center Improvements
Filter escalations to just the last 24 hours for quick daily review. Escalations now appear in the All Topics view, chat type filtering works correctly, and the topic volume chart shows more data at a glance.
Live Automation Rate
The automation rate display now shows your current live rate instead of a rolling average, giving you a more accurate picture of how your AI is performing right now.
Smarter Agent Scheduling
Agent selection now uses a least-loaded algorithm — agents with fewer active bookings get priority instead of random assignment. Schedule boundaries are enforced so agents can't be booked outside their availability, and scheduled workflows now scan all contacts without a cap.
Multi-Select Workflow Filters
Workflow group conditions now support multi-select with contains/not-contains operators, letting you build more precise audience targeting. Manual workflow runs are capped at 100 contacts to prevent accidental mass actions.
Search Improvements
Booking request status now appears in search results with a "belongs to contact" field for better context, and search now works correctly for workspaces with more than 100 listings.

Get Started
MCP Server
Connect ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, Cursor, VS Code, or any Model Context Protocol client to your Conduit workspace.
Conduit’s MCP server is available on the
v3 plan
. Contact
support@conduit.ai
to enable it for your workspace.
​
Overview
The
Model Context Protocol
is an open standard that lets AI assistants connect to external systems. Conduit’s MCP server exposes your contacts, conversations, tickets, calls, knowledge base, and agents as tools any MCP-compatible client can call.
Once connected, your AI client can:
Look up contacts, conversations, tickets, calls, reservations, and appointments
Search the knowledge base and read knowledge nodes
Send messages on a conversation or ticket, or to a contact on a specific channel
Inspect and control connected locks, thermostats, sensors, and cameras when the Devices add-on is enabled
Create and manage agents, skills, custom code tools, and contact custom attributes
Manage the Operator’s skills (
operatorSettings.skills
), separate from regular agent skills
List workspaces your token has access to
The server implements the MCP specification revision
2025-06-18
over
streamable HTTP
.
​
MCP Endpoint
https://api.conduit.ai/v1/mcp
Every request includes an
Authorization: Bearer <token>
header. Workspace-scoped tools (most of them) also require a
workspace_id
argument.
​
Authentication
Two token types are accepted. Pick the one that matches the client.
OAuth 2.1
Interactive clients that want a user-consent flow, for example Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Claude Code, or Codex. Supports Dynamic Client Registration, so no pre-provisioning is needed.
API token
Server-to-server, CI, or CLI use. Generate a
capi_...
token under
Settings > API & MCP
and paste it into the client’s bearer-token field.
​
OAuth 2.1
Conduit’s MCP server advertises itself as an OAuth 2.1 protected resource per
RFC 9728
. When a client first POSTs to the MCP endpoint without a token, the server responds with
401
and a
WWW-Authenticate
header pointing at the resource metadata document. Any spec-compliant client will discover the rest automatically.
Metadata
URL
Protected resource metadata
https://api.conduit.ai/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/v1/mcp
Authorization server
https://base.conduit.ai/oauth/mcp
Authorization server metadata
https://base.conduit.ai/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/oauth/mcp
Scopes
mcp:read
,
mcp:write
,
offline_access
Dynamic Client Registration (
RFC 7591
) is enabled, so clients register themselves on first connect. You sign in with your Conduit account in the browser window the client opens, pick which workspaces to grant access to, and the client caches the resulting access and refresh tokens.
​
API tokens
API tokens start with the
capi_
prefix and carry either
read-only
or
read/write
access. Write tools (
send_conversation_message
,
patch_contact
,
create_agent
, etc.) require a read/write token. Rotate or revoke tokens under
Settings > API & MCP
at any time.
curl
-X
POST
https://api.conduit.ai/v1/mcp
\
-H
"Authorization: Bearer capi_YOUR_TOKEN"
\
-H
"Content-Type: application/json"
\
-H
"Accept: application/json, text/event-stream"
\
-d
'{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"curl","version":"1.0"}}}'

add

​
Production Setup
Four practices that keep MCP usage safe and predictable in real workflows.
​
Pin a workspace at the start of each session
Almost every tool requires a
workspace_id
. Open each session by anchoring the model to one workspace:
Use list_workspaces and operate on the "acme-hotels" workspace for the rest of this conversation.
The model holds onto that ID in context. Subsequent prompts don’t need to repeat it. Without this anchor, the model may guess at workspace IDs or call
list_workspaces
repeatedly.
​
Keep approvals on for write tools
Read tools are safe to pre-approve in clients that support it. Write tools — anything starting with
send_
,
patch_
,
create_
,
update_
, or
delete_
— should always prompt. Each Conduit tool advertises a
destructiveHint
annotation; well-behaved clients surface it on the approval dialog.
A misfired model decision against an allow-listed
send_conversation_message
ships a real message to a real customer. Don’t allow-list it.
​
Pass an idempotency key on every send
Every write tool accepts an
idempotency_key
input (or
Idempotency-Key
HTTP header). Pass a stable UUID per logical send. Clients retry on transient failures, and without a key a retry double-sends.
{
"name"
:
"send_conversation_message"
,
"arguments"
: {
"workspace_id"
:
"wp_..."
,
"conversation_id"
:
"cv_..."
,
"body"
:
"Hi! Quick update on your booking."
,
"idempotency_key"
:
"9f2c3d1a-..."
}
}
Either tell the model to generate one per send, or set it as a project rule that gets injected into every session.
​
Use least-privilege API tokens
For non-interactive use cases (CI, server-to-server, scripts), generate a
read-only
capi_
token and use it everywhere reads are sufficient. Only generate a
read_write
token for the specific session that needs writes, and rotate it after. Tokens are revoked under
Settings > API & MCP
and take effect immediately.
​
Example Prompts
Generic starting points that work in any MCP-enabled client. Swap names and IDs for your own.
Triage open tickets
For the acme-hotels workspace, list every open helpdesk ticket touched in the last 24 hours,
group them by inferred topic, and tell me the three most urgent ones with the customer name
and a one-line summary.
Uses
list_helpdesk_tickets
,
get_helpdesk_ticket
,
list_ticket_messages
. All read-only — no approval prompts if those tools are pre-approved.
Reproduce a customer report
Search the acme-hotels workspace for any conversation where the contact mentioned
"double charge" in the last week. Pull the full message thread for the most recent
one and show me the timestamps.
Useful in terminal-based clients (Claude Code, Codex) where you can immediately jump from the conversation into the relevant code path.
Draft a reply with full context
Pull conversation cv_abc on the acme-hotels workspace. Read the last twenty messages.
Draft a reply that addresses the refund question, matches the tone of our previous
responses, and cites our refund policy from the knowledge base. Don't send it — just print it.
The “don’t send” constraint is the safety belt while iterating. Drop it when you’re ready and the model will call
send_conversation_message
, which prompts for approval before anything ships.
Audit a knowledge base section
Search the knowledge base for any node that mentions our old cancellation policy
("48 hours"). For each match, show me the node title, the path, and the sentence
that contains the phrase.
Pair with a follow-up that calls
update_knowledge_node
(write tool, prompts for approval) once you’ve reviewed the list.
​
Rate Limits and Errors
By default, MCP tool calls are limited to
120 requests per minute per workspace
and share the same workspace-level budget as REST API requests. A
429
response includes a
Retry-After
header. Error responses follow the MCP spec:
content[0].text
holds the error message and
isError: true
is set on tool results.
See
Rate Limits
for details.
Status
Meaning
401
Missing, expired, or revoked token
403
Token does not have access to the requested workspace, or lacks
read_write
for a write tool
404
Resource not found in the given workspace
429
Rate limit exceeded
​

The

tools manage the
Operator’s
skills (the knowledge cards the Operator assistant uses), which are separate from the regular agent skills managed by
*_skill
. They read and write
operatorSettings.skills
with the same workspace scoping and
Manage Agents
permission as the Operator settings screen in the app, and they are MCP-only (there is no matching REST route). Every
operator_*
tool takes a required
workspace_id
; writes need a read/write token and the
Manage Agents
permission.
The portal tools read guest sessions and build verification rules, offers, and page templates for the Portals add-on. They need the add-on enabled plus
Access Portals
for reads and
Manage Portals
for writes. See the
Portals API reference
for session submissions, step types, layout blocks, and worked examples.
The device tools require the Devices add-on. Read tools can inspect device state and history; write tools can manage access codes, locks, thermostats, noise thresholds, and property mappings. Device actions also follow workspace policy and contact scope. See
Devices
for supported locks, agent behavior, and the full tool guide.
See the
REST API reference
for the underlying resource shapes. MCP tools share the same schemas.
To author a custom tool over MCP, call
list_custom_tool_runtimes
first. It returns the entrypoint signature, required return shape, and available dependencies for Python and JavaScript, so the model writes
code
that passes validation on the first try. See the
Custom Tools overview
for the full contract.
​
Troubleshooting
Claude shows Request instead of Connect
On a Claude Team plan, members without permission to enable connectors see a
Request
button for Conduit instead of
Connect
. Click
Request
to send the connector to your organization’s admins for review. The button changes to
Requested
while approval is pending. An admin must approve the connector before you can connect it.
See Claude’s
guide to requesting a connector on a Team plan
for more details.
Client says Unauthorized after working for a while
The OAuth access token expired and the client does not have a refresh token. Disconnect and reconnect the server. If you’re using an API token, it may have been rotated or revoked. Check
Settings > API & MCP
.
list_workspaces returns an empty array
The token is valid but not scoped to any workspace. For OAuth, remove the Conduit connector in your client and reconnect, making sure to grant at least one workspace during consent. For API tokens, confirm the token is attached to the right workspace.
Write tool returns 403
API tokens default to read-only. Create a new token with read/write access, or use an OAuth client where you consented to the
mcp:write
scope.
Client cannot discover the OAuth server
Some clients do not support Dynamic Client Registration or do not follow the
WWW-Authenticate
resource metadata pointer. In that case, use an API token instead, or point the client directly at the authorization server URLs in the
Authentication
section.
No tools showing up after connecting
The connection succeeded but the client hasn’t refreshed its tool list. Disconnect and reconnect, or restart the client. In Claude Code, run
/mcp
to force a reconnect.

Conduit API
Programmatic access to your Conduit workspace data.
The Conduit API is only available on the
v3 plan
. Contact
support@conduit.ai
to enable API access for your workspace.
​
Overview
The Conduit API gives you programmatic access to contacts, conversations, tickets, calls, escalations, custom attributes, knowledge base, and workspace metadata. Read and write endpoints are available depending on your token’s access level. All endpoints are REST-based and return JSON.
Base URL
https://api.conduit.ai/v1
​
Authentication
All requests require a
Bearer token
in the
Authorization
header. Generate API tokens from
Settings > API & MCP
. The setting is personal, so tokens can grant access to one or more workspaces where you are an admin.
curl
https://api.conduit.ai/v1/workspaces
\
-H
"Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN"
Tokens are scoped to one or more workspaces. Use the
List Workspaces
endpoint to discover which workspaces your token can access.
​
Pagination
List endpoints return paginated results. Use
limit
(1-100, default 20) and
cursor
to page through results.
{
"data"
: [
...
],
"next_cursor"
:
"page-token"
,
"has_more"
:
true
}
Pass
next_cursor
as the
cursor
query parameter in your next request to fetch the next page. When
has_more
is
false
, you’ve reached the end.
​
Polling for new activity
Cursors page through a result set once. Keeping an external system in sync needs the opposite: only what has changed since you last looked. Two timestamp filters cover that.
1
Find threads that moved
Call
List Conversations
with
updated_after
set to the highest
updated_at
you have already stored.
GET /v1/conversations?workspace_id=WS&updated_after=2026-04-03T03:15:04.000Z
2
Fetch only the new messages in each thread
For each conversation returned, call
List Conversation Messages
with
created_after
set to the highest
created_at
you have stored for that thread. This replaces re-paging the whole transcript.
GET /v1/conversations/{id}/messages?created_after=2026-04-03T03:15:04.000Z
Both filters are inclusive (at or after), and
created_at
is truncated to the millisecond, so the message on the boundary is normally returned again. Deduplicate on the message
id
rather than assuming every result is new.
created_after
filters on
created_at
(when Conduit recorded the message), not
sent_at
(when the channel says it was sent). Those differ for messages imported from a connected channel, and only
created_at
moves forward as Conduit observes messages, so it is the safe watermark. Using
sent_at
as your cursor will eventually skip a backdated import.
​
Telling AI replies from operator replies
Every message carries
is_sent_by_autopilot
. It is
true
only when Conduit’s AI agent generated and sent the message, and
false
for operator replies, workflow sends, and messages ingested from a connected channel’s own UI.
Use the flag directly. Do not infer automation from
sender.user_id
: AI sends usually leave it
null
, but so do host replies typed in an OTA’s own UI and messages sent by workflows, and a small number of AI sends do carry a user id.
​
Rate Limits
By default, API requests are limited to
120 requests per minute per workspace
. If you exceed the limit, the API returns
429 Too Many Requests
with a
Retry-After
header indicating when you can retry. Some workspaces may have higher limits based on plan or entitlement.
See
Rate Limits
for details.
​
Errors
All errors return a JSON object with an
error
field:
{
"error"
:
"Invalid workspace id"
}
Status
Meaning
400
Invalid request parameters
401
Missing or invalid API token
403
Token does not have access to the requested workspace
404
Resource not found
429
Rate limit exceeded

ABOUT:
Canbnb is a property management company based in Canberra, Australia, specializing in Airbnb and short-term accommodation management.
FOUNDED:
2017
USING CONDUIT SINCE:
March 2024
“Everything is right where we need it. We’re not scrambling anymore. We’re in control.”
Jo-Anne Quiros
Process and Communication Manager, Canbnb
In the early days, Jo’s morning routine was simple. Running a lean operation at Canbnb meant she handled all guest communications herself, responding to emails and messages while juggling last-minute bookings. Two freelance cleaners managed turnovers, and when things got busy, even the owner pitched in to clean properties.
It wasn’t perfect, but it worked.
Then, growth hit.
From 7 properties to 170, the pace was relentless. What had once been a manageable workflow quickly turned into a daily scramble to keep up. Guest messages overflowed, on-site teams struggled to stay aligned with the growing virtual support staff, and small inefficiencies began compounding into operational bottlenecks.
The Challenge
One morning, Jo logged in to find 630 unread messages—some from guests, some from cleaners, and a few urgent ones from owners. By the time she triaged the inbox, a check-in issue had already escalated into a full refund request. “We were moving too slow,” she recalled. “And at that scale, slow is expensive.”
Logging into multiple platforms, cross-referencing guest requests with cleaner schedules, answering urgent owner inquiries, all while making sure nothing slipped through the cracks, Jo’s morning routine was no longer no longer sustainable.
The stress of managing scale without the right infrastructure was mounting. Canbnb needed a system that could keep up with their growth—
without breaking their operations.
“We couldn’t run things the same way anymore,” Jo recalls. “The volume of messages and tasks was overwhelming, and the disconnect between virtual and on-site teams was creating inefficiencies we couldn’t ignore.”
Their operational challenges boiled down to three key problems:
Virtual vs. On-Site Coordination
– Remote support staff and on-the-ground teams needed to work in sync, but managing that balance at scale became increasingly difficult.
Response Time and Guest Experience
– With more properties came more inquiries. Slow response times meant unhappy guests, and scattered systems made it harder to track urgent issues.
Onboarding Complexity
– Property management software is notoriously difficult to implement at scale. With 170+ properties, switching systems felt like a high-risk, high-friction move.
Jo and Dan, the company’s leadership team, knew they needed a better solution—but they weren’t convinced AI was the answer.
The Skepticism
The buzz around AI in hospitality was everywhere, but Jo remained skeptical.
“I’m in operations every day. I see the gaps in these systems. AI sounded promising, but I wasn’t convinced it could really fit into our workflow.”
Dan, however, saw the bigger picture. As Canbnb pushed toward their next growth milestone, he knew they needed a platform that could do more than just streamline messaging. It had to be their central system—the foundation for everything from guest interactions to team coordination.
Their biggest hesitation? Onboarding. Property management systems are notoriously difficult to migrate, and the last thing they wanted was a drawn-out, complicated transition.
But when they set up Conduit, their doubts quickly disappeared.
The Shift
“Honestly, setting up Conduit was one of the easiest things I’ve ever done,” Jo admits. "Compared to other property management platforms, which often require weeks (or even months) to fully integrate, HostAI was up and running in a fraction of the time.”
More than just ease of use, it was that it fit into their existing operations:
A structured inbox
made it easier to monitor guest inquiries and escalate urgent issues before they became problems.
Multi-Channel Integration
– Conduit connected seamlessly with Hostaway, WhatsApp, Email, SMS, and a Chat Widget, consolidating all interactions into a single interface.
Dedicated Inboxes
– Canbnb structured their team’s workflow with separate Guest, Owner, and Vendor inboxes, ensuring the right teams handled the right conversations.
AI as the voice & tone guide
– Instead of training each new hire manually, Conduit enforced brand-aligned responses and company policies automatically.
The Transformation
Once onboarded, Jo saw a shift in her team’s mindset.
“We’re no longer just answering messages—we’re editing and guiding our AI assistant. The cognitive load has dropped, and each guest services rep is 10x more impactful.”
More importantly:
Automating at Scale
– Conduit now helps Canbnb send roughly
1,500 messages per week
, with
60% handled by AI
.
Operations became streamlined
– No more scattered attention across platforms. Remote agents could see exactly what on-site teams needed in real time.
Guest interactions improved
– AI-assisted replies ensured that every guest received timely, accurate responses, even during peak hours.
Company policies were reinforced
– AI suggestions kept human agents aligned with company standards, reducing errors and inconsistencies.
Better visibility into guest issues
– Conduit's built-in reporting helped them track
the most common guest concerns
, allowing them to address root causes proactively.
One of the biggest wins? The ability to track and act on guest feedback more effectively. Conduit's review dashboard gave them a real-time pulse on guest satisfaction, allowing them to marry guest reviews with cleaner performance and reservation data.
Conduit didn’t just improve efficiency—it
became the connective tissue
between their virtual and on-site teams.
The Outcome
Today, Canbnb isn’t just using Conduit—they’re building their future on it.
“We see Conduit as our central platform,” Dan says. "As we push past 200 properties, it’s not just about keeping up—it’s about scaling the right way, without losing control of our operations.”
With AI reducing friction, streamlining communication, and reinforcing company standards, Canbnb is moving toward its next phase of growth with clarity, not chaos.
And as for Jo? The morning routine looks a little different now.
“It’s just…easier,” she says. “Everything is right where we need it. We’re not scrambling anymore. We’re in control.”

Connect PMS
Connect PMS
Connect your property management system to Conduit to sync booking data, create contacts, and power AI responses.
​
Overview
Conduit operates fully horizontally across industries. For hospitality and property management teams, connecting your Property Management System brings property and booking data into the platform. The system automatically creates contacts from reservations and facilitates communication. Conduit integrates with over 15 different PMS systems to populate listing information.
​
Setup Steps
The initial configuration process involves four main steps:
Airbnb can be the workspace’s primary PMS or an additional messaging
connection. To use it as your PMS, select Airbnb from
Add PMS
or choose
Use Airbnb as your PMS
under
Settings > Connections > Airbnb
. See
Connect Airbnb
for both connection types.
Navigate to
Settings > Connections > PMS
If PMS isn’t visible, create a new workspace and select either
Short Term
Rental
or
Long Term Rental
under Advanced settings
Select your business’s PMS provider
Complete the provider’s authentication steps. Airbnb uses an authorization
window instead of an account ID and API key.
Your listings and PMS-backed content will appear in
Build > Knowledge
after sync completes.
​
Schedule PMS Knowledge Sync
After importing listings, turn on auto-sync to keep their PMS-backed Knowledge
current:
Open
Knowledge
from the main sidebar.
Click
Sources
at the bottom of the Knowledge sidebar.
Open your PMS source.
Open the three-dot menu, choose
Set auto-sync
, then select
Daily
,
Weekly
,
Every 2 weeks
, or
Monthly
.
The schedule applies to the whole PMS integration. It refreshes Knowledge for
listings already imported into Conduit. To find and import a property added to
your PMS later, use
Check for new listings
from the same PMS source menu.
Choosing a schedule does not run a sync immediately. Use
Sync knowledge
for
an immediate refresh, and open
Sync history
to review past and upcoming
syncs. See
Auto-sync Knowledge Sources
for screenshots,
status meanings, paused-sync recovery, and how to turn auto-sync off.
​
Connection Rules
Conduit prevents connection combinations that could create duplicate guest
conversations.
You can connect multiple PMS accounts when they use the same messaging
setup. PMS providers that deliver guest messages cannot share a workspace
with providers that only supply property and reservation data.
When you choose another PMS, incompatible providers are disabled. Use a
separate workspace if you need both types.
If Airbnb is your primary property management connection, you cannot connect
another PMS.
You can connect Airbnb directly alongside a PMS. If the PMS handles guest
messages, those messages continue through the PMS. If it does not, Conduit
can receive Airbnb messages directly and match them to PMS reservations. See
Connect Airbnb
for setup instructions.
If your workspace already has both PMS types, you can reconnect an existing
account to refresh its credentials, but you cannot add another PMS until the
conflict is resolved.
​
Messaging Support by PMS
Conduit classifies each PMS connection by whether it sends guest messages to
Conduit. This describes the Conduit integration, not every messaging feature the
PMS vendor may offer.
“Non-messaging” does not mean that guest messaging is unsupported in Conduit.
It means messaging is not supported natively through that PMS connection.
Conduit supports messaging for those PMS providers through auxiliary channel
connections, such as direct Airbnb and Expedia connections.
Connection type
PMS providers
How guest messages reach Conduit
Messaging
Beds24, Guesty, Hospitable, Hostaway, Hostfully, Hostify, Lodgify, OwnerRez, PassTheKeys, Resly, Smily
The PMS sends guest messages to Conduit. Keep OTA messaging routed through the PMS. Connecting the same OTA directly can create duplicate conversations.
Non-messaging
Apaleo, CiiRUS, Cloudbeds, Escapia, Homhero, Kross Booking, Mews, Opera Cloud, RMS, Streamline, Track
The PMS supplies property and reservation data but does not send guest messages to Conduit natively. Messaging is supported through auxiliary connections, so connect each OTA messaging channel directly to Conduit.
For example, Cloudbeds syncs Expedia reservations but does not send Expedia
messages to Conduit. To receive those messages in the Conduit inbox, contact
Conduit support to connect the Expedia properties directly. Expedia messaging
uses a shared connection managed by Conduit, so there are no workspace
credentials to enter.
Connecting Expedia messaging to Conduit does not disconnect Expedia from
Cloudbeds. Cloudbeds continues to manage inventory, rates, availability, and
reservation sync. Only Expedia guest messaging is routed directly to Conduit.
Do not keep messaging enabled through both Cloudbeds and Conduit, because the
same conversation could arrive twice.
Airbnb is handled separately from these PMS groups. Follow
Connect
Airbnb
to use Airbnb as your PMS, manage
the primary account, or add direct Airbnb messaging accounts.
​
Opera Cloud Connection Instructions
Oracle OPERA Cloud connects through the Oracle Hospitality Integration Platform
(OHIP) and needs five values from the OHIP Developer Portal rather than a single
API key. It has its own page:
Connect Opera Cloud
.
​
Lodgify Connection Instructions
Lodgify connects with a single
API key
. There’s no OAuth redirect and no
account ID, paste the key, Conduit pulls in your properties, and you pick which
listings to import.
​
Part 1: Get your Lodgify API key
Log in to
Lodgify
and open the
Menu
in the top right, then click
Settings
.
Select
Public API
in the settings menu.
Click the copy button next to your API key. That key is your access token, it has both read and write permissions. Keep it private.
If the Public API page doesn’t show a key, your plan may not include API
access yet. Request access from that page or contact Lodgify support.
​
Part 2: Connect Lodgify in Conduit
1
Open the PMS connection screen
In Conduit, go to
Settings > Connections > PMS
and click
Connect PMS
.
If PMS isn’t visible, your workspace needs to be a
Short Term Rental
or
Hotel
type. Set the industry under the workspace’s company settings, or
create a new workspace of that type.
2
Pick Lodgify from the provider list
Search for
Lodgify
and click it.
3
Paste your API key and connect
Paste the API key you copied from Lodgify into the
API Key
field and click
Connect
.
4
Import your listings
Conduit fetches your Lodgify properties and shows how many it found. Click
Import
to bring them in (or
Skip
to connect without importing yet).
The import runs in the background and can take a few minutes.
Once the sync finishes, your listings and PMS-backed content appear under
Build > Knowledge
, and new reservations start creating contacts
automatically.
​
Beds24 Connection Instructions
​
Part 1: Authentication
Open
Settings > Connections > PMS
in Conduit and click the Beds24 logo to reach the authentication screen
Select “Select all” on all three checkboxes, then click “Generate Invite Code”
Copy the invite code and paste it back on the authentication screen
Click “Connect” and wait for the success confirmation message
​
Part 2: Messaging Setup
In Conduit, open your completed Beds24 connection and copy the
Webhook URL
field
Open the Beds24 app and navigate to Settings > Properties > Access
In the Booking Webhooks section, select “2 - with personal data” as the webhook version
Paste the Conduit Webhook URL into the URL field
Leave the Custom Header empty and click “Save”
Repeat this process for each property in your Beds24 account

ABOUT:
We are reimagining the idea of 'home' from something fixed to something flexible and simplifying the rental process for both landlords and tenants as we go.
FOUNDED:
2019
USING CONDUIT SINCE:
December 2023
“Within our niche of property management, we wanted to tackle as many goals as possible...the only thing we wouldn’t bother to do is what you guys do.”
Michael Buggy
CEO, The Flex
Two years ago, Flex Living was like many fast-growing operators, juggling a stack of tools, rising support volume, and increasingly fragmented data. Today, they’re building toward a future with just two systems: one for operations, one for AI.
Here’s how a modern rental platform became a full-stack AI company, and why Conduit is one of only two platforms they still need.
The Challenge
When Flex Living launched, it was lean, fast, and human-powered. But as the company scaled across cities like London, San Francisco, and Dubai, that model broke down.
“We were using 17 different SaaS platforms at one point,” said Michael Buggy, CEO. “The cost adds up, and it makes everything really inefficient because the platforms don’t speak to each other.”
Fragmentation is both costly and limiting. Different tools created data silos. Tasks couldn’t be automated. Support agents had to bounce between inboxes, project management tools, and CRMs just to resolve basic issues. Scaling the business meant scaling headcount.
And none of it felt sustainable.
The tipping point came when Flex Living decided to build its own property management system from scratch. They were replacing 17 disconnected SaaS tools with a unified platform tailored to their workflow. But there was one category they deliberately left out: communication.
“Within our niche of property management, we wanted to tackle as many goals as possible,” Michael explained. “The only thing we wouldn’t bother to do is what you guys do conversational AI.”
Building high-quality AI communication, from inbox to escalation logic, requires a different kind of infrastructure and a level of precision they knew would be hard to replicate in-house. Rather than dilute their focus, they chose to partner with a team already years ahead in that domain. That’s when they turned to Conduit.
The Solution
Flex Living partnered with Conduit to overhaul how they handled guest communication. This meant everything from automating frontline messaging to improving visibility across conversations. Conduit’s AI agents connected directly to their property data, resolving common issues autonomously and escalating when needed.
“70% automation of customer service is very realistic,” Michael said. “It’s achievable based on where we’re at today, not even based on where we’re going to be in a year’s time.”
At first, Michael hesitated to switch on the AI. He was worried it would get things wrong or confuse guests. But the turning point came when he understood how Conduit was designed.
If the information wasn’t there, the AI wouldn’t reply. If it was there, it would. That failure of understanding created a sense of fear to switch the AI on. Had I known that it wasn't going to do things that I had not told it to do, I would have felt much more comfortable switching it on sooner.
Flex Living’s rollout wasn’t frictionless. One early mistake was assigning the onboarding to someone without the technical context needed to structure the knowledge base. In retrospect, Michael said it should’ve been founder-led, or supported by a tool that made setup simple.
Despite the initial bumps, the team quickly aligned. Agents weren’t being replaced. They were being refocused.
“I think that hesitation sort of disappeared when they realized that what Conduit was doing was serving the customers and then enabling them to follow up where the real problems were. So it was giving them more time to solve real problems and less time spent on doing stuff that didn't need to be solved because the AI could easily do it.”
The Impact
Flex Living moved from reactive support to proactive operations. Instead of dealing with fragmented messages and manual escalation, the team gained real-time visibility into what guests needed and how the business was performing.
Favorite features include:
Call summaries that condense 30-minute conversations into 10 bullet points
Conversation tagging to quickly identify issues like cleaning or maintenance
A unified inbox with both phone and messaging support
Key Results:
70%+ automation of customer support volume
Significant reduction in manual triage and agent overhead
Streamlined escalation and task management for ops teams
And unlike legacy tools, Conduit was evolving rapidly.
“On day one, Conduit was a Lamborghini,” Michael said. “Comparing for example Front to Zendesk to Trengo and so on, it was already clear on day one that you guys were light years ahead of them Trengo and Front. And I remember the first time we spoke to you guys, we instantly understood that you had the culture of a company that was going to succeed.” That speed and clarity of vision sealed the deal.
“And when it comes to AI, I don't think any of them have even come close to building something that works well. I mean, I mean they're still basically like flow bots.”
Looking Ahead
The next chapter is even more ambitious. Flex Living is nearly done building its own PMS platform to replace tools like Hostaway and Monday.com. In four months, they expect to run on just two systems: their internal ops hub and Conduit.
The goal? A world with zero system fragmentation, where 90% of tasks are automated and AI agents orchestrate the flow of work.
We’re building the ultimate product. Something that handles 80–90% of customer communication, ties into tasks, and makes it easy to know which customers need attention.
With the communication layer solved, the team can now focus on what comes next: scaling globally, shipping faster, and pushing the limits of AI-native operations.
As Michael put it: “We’re just getting started.”

The Journey
Overview
The 5 Levels of AI Automation
Conduit’s framework for understanding AI’s transformative role in customer service - from assistant to strategist, from task execution to system design.
The current conversation around AI in the workplace is broken. We’re told AI exists to “automate repetitive tasks so humans can focus on more important work,” but this framing is shallow—it treats AI as just another productivity tool.
History tells a different story. Every major leap in automation (printing press, steam engine, internet) hasn’t just replaced work; it has elevated people into new roles, transforming
what
we do,
how
we do it, and what we value.
AI represents the next leap. At Conduit, a customer service agent company that operates fully horizontally, AI’s role in customer service isn’t merely about saving time—it fundamentally changes the nature of work itself.
The framework used to map this transformation is
The 5 Levels of AI Automation
: a progression from assistant to strategist, from task execution to system design.
​
Level 0: The Co-Pilot
Where most businesses begin. The AI supports you while you maintain full control. It drafts responses, finds information, translates messages, and suggests actions—making workflows faster and smoother while you handle every conversation.
You remain in the driver’s seat; the AI is a skilled assistant, not yet a partner. Most AI software today operates at this level, though Conduit positions this as only the starting point toward full automation.
​
Level 1: The Teacher
The first real shift occurs here. You begin letting the AI handle simple, repetitive conversations end-to-end. Your role transforms from replying to teaching.
You correct mistakes, approve good work, and provide examples. Performance is measured less by conversation volume and more by how well you develop your AI “employee”—your first step into management, moving from executor to mentor.
​
Level 2: The Builder
From teaching to designing. The AI handles most conversations while performing actions: updating systems, triggering workflows, booking appointments, filing requests.
Your role becomes
design and expand
these capabilities. You create workflows, establish procedures, and connect tools and data sources so the AI acts confidently. You’re building the operational foundation the AI operates on.
​
Level 3: The AI Orchestrator
Full-scale transformation. The AI manages most conversational operations—routing messages, answering and making calls, resolving requests, escalating only when needed, driving multi-step workflows across channels.
Your job shifts from direct execution to orchestration. Like a maestro, you don’t play individual notes; you coordinate agents, tools, and processes in harmony. You hire and train people to design, monitor, and improve flows—not answer every message.
​
Level 4: The AI Director (The Future)
The interface disappears. You speak to your AI as you would a trusted executive. It manages its own growth, monitors performance, and surfaces only insights and decisions requiring your input.
It reports where the system excels, where it falls short, recommends changes, and implements them. You’ve delegated an entire business function to an autonomous operator.
​
The Journey
Moving from Level 0 to Level 4 redefines work itself:
From
task-doers
to
teachers
From
teachers
to
builders
From
builders
to
orchestrators
And ultimately, to
strategists
working alongside autonomous AI leaders
Conduit is designed to guide teams in any industry through each stage, providing tools, visibility, and control to evolve your role and business as AI becomes an integral, trusted team member.

Overview
How Conduit Agents Work
Conduit is a customer service agent company that operates fully horizontally - transparent, trainable, and fully controllable.
Conduit is a customer service agent company that operates fully horizontally, serving teams across every industry. The platform is designed to be transparent, trainable, and fully controllable, addressing a key limitation of typical AI tools by being the opposite of a “black box”—users can inspect reasoning, see sources, and make reliable updates to agent behavior.
​
Four Core System Components
​
1. Inbox — The Mouth
Unified conversation threads per contact across all channels (email, SMS, WhatsApp, voice, Airbnb, live-chat)
AI responses are transparent, showing reasoning and sources
Users can approve, edit, or teach the agent directly inline

2. Build Surfaces — The Brain
Agents

​
3. Workflows — The Arms & Legs
Three workflow types automate communication:
Proactive workflows
: Scheduled or triggered outreach
Routing workflows
: Direct details to appropriate systems or team members
Triage workflows
: Escalate to humans when needed, then auto-close
​
4. Dashboards — The Nervous System
Live metrics on automation rates, escalation reasons, and sentiment
All charts connect to raw conversations for quick adjustments
​
Deployment Model
The system works across any industry, launching with customizable playbooks and intents. Most teams go live within a week and can customize brand voice, policies, enable/disable workflows, and write custom API functions.

Getting Started
Inbox Routing
Automatically route incoming messages and calls to the right inbox
​
What is inbox routing?
When a new contact reaches out via SMS, WhatsApp, email, voice, or any other channel, Conduit needs to know which inbox to put them in. Inbox routing lets you set rules that automatically assign contacts to a specific inbox based on the channel they came from.
Without routing rules, new contacts land in the
Unmapped
inbox, where your team would need to manually move them to the correct inbox.
​
How it works
A new message or call comes in from a channel (e.g., an SMS to your Twilio number)
Conduit checks if there’s a routing rule for that channel
If a rule matches
, the contact is automatically placed in the target inbox
If no rule matches
, the contact stays in the Unmapped inbox
Routing only applies to
new, unmapped contacts
. If a contact is already assigned to an inbox (from a reservation, manual assignment, etc.), routing rules won’t change their inbox.
​
Supported channels
You can create routing rules for any connected channel:
Channel
Routed by
SMS
Phone number
WhatsApp
Phone number
Email
Email address or account
Voice
Phone number
Messenger
Facebook page
Instagram
Instagram account
Helpdesk
Third-party connection
Slack
Slack channel
Widget
Chat widget
​
Setting up a routing rule
1
Go to Settings > Inbox Routing
Navigate to
Settings > Inbox Routing
in your workspace.
2
Click Add Rule
Click the
Add rule
button to create a new routing rule.
3
Select a channel
Choose the channel you want to route from the dropdown. Only channels that don’t already have a routing rule will appear.
4
Select a target inbox
Choose which inbox contacts from this channel should be routed to.
5
Save
Save the rule. It takes effect immediately for new incoming contacts.
When you create a rule for a phone number, Conduit automatically applies the rule to all channel types on that number (SMS, voice, WhatsApp). You don’t need to create separate rules for each.
​
Editing and deleting rules
To
edit
a rule, click the edit button on the rule and change the target inbox. The channel itself can’t be changed after creation.
To
delete
a rule, click the delete button. Contacts already routed by that rule stay in their current inbox.
​
The Unmapped inbox
The Unmapped inbox is a catch-all for contacts that don’t match any routing rule. You can:
View and manage unmapped contacts like any other inbox
Manually move contacts to the correct inbox
Create routing rules to prevent contacts from landing here in the future
​
Routing and workflows
Routing rules run before workflow triggers.
When a message or call comes in, Conduit routes the contact to the correct inbox first, then evaluates workflow triggers. This means your workflow triggers should target the
routed inbox
, not the Unmapped inbox.
For example, if you have a routing rule that sends voice calls to the “Customer” inbox, a “Call completed” workflow trigger should be configured for the “Customer” inbox.
